 `./docs/tools/office-viewers.md`

```text
1	# View Office Documents in the Terminal
2	
3	Open and preview Microsoft Office (`.docx` / `.xlsx` / `.pptx`), legacy binary (`.doc` / `.xls` / `.ppt`), and OpenDocument (`.odt` / `.ods` / `.odp`) files without leaving the terminal — no Microsoft Office, no GUI.
4	
5	There is no single tool that views everything well, so this repo wires a small **per-format + two-mode** stack behind one dispatcher, [`view-office`](#the-view-office-dispatcher), and hooks it into the [yazi](tmux/README.md) file manager for inline previews.
6	
7	## TL;DR
8	
9	| Format | Interactive (TUI / pager) | Quick preview (stdout) |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| Word `.docx` | [`doxx`](https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx) | `doxx --export ansi` |
12	| Excel `.xlsx` | [`visidata`](https://www.visidata.org/) (`vd`) | `markitdown \| glow` |
13	| PowerPoint `.pptx` | `markitdown \| glow` (pager) | `markitdown \| glow` |
14	| Legacy `.doc/.xls/.ppt`, OpenDocument `.odt/.ods/.odp`, `.rtf` | LibreOffice → OOXML twin → above | same, converted first |
15	
16	```console
17	$ view-office report.docx                 # interactive: rich TUI (doxx)
18	$ view-office --preview budget.xlsx        # markdown/ANSI to stdout
19	$ view-office legacy-memo.doc              # LibreOffice converts, then doxx
20	```
21	
22	## The `view-office` dispatcher
23	
24	`view-office` (source: `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office`, deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/`, on `PATH`) is a small bash script that dispatches by file extension:
25	
26	```text
27	view-office [--preview] [--width N] FILE
28	  -p, --preview    render to stdout (ANSI/markdown) instead of launching a TUI
29	  -w, --width N    wrap width for --preview (default: $COLUMNS or 100)
30	  -h, --help       show help
31	```
32	
33	Two modes:
34	
35	- **Interactive** (default) — launches the best full-screen viewer for the type: `doxx` for Word, `visidata` for Excel, a `glow` pager for PowerPoint.
36	- **Preview** (`--preview`) — emits ANSI/markdown to stdout. This is the single source of truth that the [yazi previewer](#yazi-inline-previews) (and any future `tv` / `fzf` integration) calls, so preview logic lives in exactly one place.
37	
38	Legacy binary and OpenDocument formats are converted to their modern OOXML twin with **LibreOffice headless** into a temp dir, then re-dispatched to the handler above (e.g. `.doc → .docx → doxx`). Missing tools produce an actionable install hint and exit 2 — nothing fails silently.
39	
40	> **Why bash, not the `uv run --script` pattern** used by `pqsum`/`yth`/`mlf`? `view-office` sits on yazi's preview hot-path (invoked on every file hover). uv/Python startup (~100–200 ms) would make previews feel laggy; bash dispatch is ~5 ms.
41	
42	## The tools
43	
44	### doxx — terminal-native Word viewer
45	
46	[doxx](https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx) renders `.docx` directly in the terminal: bold/italic/headings, smart tables, LaTeX equations, and inline images (Kitty/iTerm2/Sixel). It also exports non-interactively — `doxx FILE --export ansi|markdown|text|csv|json` — which is what `view-office --preview` uses for Word.
47	
48	- **macOS:** `brew install doxx` (it's in **homebrew-core** — the README's `bgreenwell/tap/doxx` is stale; that tap ships `xleak`/`lstr`, not doxx).
49	- **Linux:** GitHub release `.tar.xz` (cargo-dist, static musl on x86_64) → `~/.local/bin/doxx`, installed by the `devtools` ansible role.
50	
51	### visidata — spreadsheet multitool
52	
53	Already in the repo (see [Data Viewers](../shells/aliases.md)). `vd file.xlsx` opens a fast, vim-keyed TUI over the sheet. Used for **interactive** Excel; for previews, `markitdown` renders the sheet to a markdown table instead (visidata is TUI-only).
54	
55	### markitdown — Office → Markdown
56	
57	[Microsoft MarkItDown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown) converts `.docx/.xlsx/.pptx` (and more) to Markdown, optimized for LLM/RAG pipelines. It is the universal preview engine for Excel and PowerPoint here, because **pandoc cannot read `.pptx` or `.xlsx`** (pandoc only *writes* pptx; it reads docx/odt/epub but not the spreadsheet/presentation formats). Installed as a uv tool (`python_uv_tools`).
58	
59	> **Gotcha:** the bare `markitdown` package ships **no format converters** — they live in optional extras. This repo installs `markitdown[docx,xlsx,pptx]`; without the extras every Office file raises `MissingDependencyException`. (Not `[all]` — that adds pdf/audio/youtube/azure bloat.)
60	
61	### LibreOffice — legacy-format fallback
62	
63	Only `soffice --headless --convert-to` can read the old binary formats (`.doc/.xls/.ppt`) and OpenDocument. Heavy (~hundreds of MB), so it's a **fallback**, installed by `devtools` (macOS cask / `libreoffice-writer,calc,impress` on Debian with recommends off). On macOS `soffice` is not on `PATH`; `view-office` resolves the `.app` bundle path itself. No-root Linux installs skip it and `view-office` prints an install hint for legacy files.
64	
65	## Yazi inline previews
66	
67	Hovering an Office file in [yazi](tmux/README.md) renders a preview in the right pane. This is the repo's first yazi **plugin** integration, via the [`ya pkg`](#the-ya-pkg-plugin-mechanism) manager and the [`piper.yazi`](https://github.com/yazi-rs/plugins/tree/main/piper.yazi) plugin ("pipe any shell command as a previewer"):
68	
69	```toml
70	# dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml
71	[plugin]
72	prepend_previewers = [
73	  { url = "*.docx", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
74	  # … .xlsx .pptx .doc .xls .ppt .odt .ods .odp .rtf
75	]
76	```
77	
78	`piper.yazi` passes `$w` (preview width) and `$1` (file path); the command's stdout becomes the preview. The `run` string and `view-office`'s `--preview`/`--width` interface are a **contract** — change one, change the other.
79	
80	### The `ya pkg` plugin mechanism
81	
82	`ya pkg` is Yazi's plugin manager (`ya` is the CLI companion shipped with yazi). It clones a plugin, copies it into `~/.config/yazi/plugins/`, and locks its version in `~/.config/yazi/package.toml`.
83	
84	In this repo the lockfile is **chezmoi-managed** (`dot_config/yazi/package.toml`) and the plugins are materialized by a hash-gated run-script:
85	
86	| Piece | Path | Role |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| Lockfile (SSOT) | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml` | pins `yazi-rs/plugins:piper` (rev + hash) |
89	| Installer | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` | runs `ya pkg install` when the lockfile changes |
90	| Previewer wiring | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin]` | maps Office extensions → `piper -- view-office …` |
91	
92	`ya pkg install` **reads but never rewrites** `package.toml`, so there's no chezmoi drift. It is install-only by design (like the rest of the repo) — bump plugin versions with `ya pkg upgrade` (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`), then copy the regenerated `~/.config/yazi/package.toml` back into the source.
93	
94	Add another yazi plugin:
95	
96	```bash
97	ya pkg add <owner>/<repo>:<plugin>       # installs + updates ~/.config/yazi/package.toml
98	cp ~/.config/yazi/package.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/yazi/package.toml)"
99	```
100	
101	## Where things live
102	
103	| Surface | Path |
104	|---|---|
105	| Dispatcher CLI | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office` |
106	| Completions (zsh/bash) | `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/55_view_office_completion.*` |
107	| doxx / LibreOffice install | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
108	| markitdown install | `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` |
109	| yazi previewers | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` |
110	| yazi plugin lockfile + installer | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` |
111	| Upgrades | `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`) |
112	
113	## Gotchas
114	
115	- **`markitdown` needs extras** — see the box above. `markitdown[docx,xlsx,pptx]`, not bare `markitdown`.
116	- **pandoc ≠ Office reader** — it cannot read `.pptx`/`.xlsx`. Use `markitdown` for those. (pandoc still powers the [web reader](web-reader.md) for HTML.)
117	- **Uppercase extensions** — the yazi `url` globs are lowercase (`*.docx`); a file named `Report.DOCX` won't trigger the previewer (running `view-office` directly still works — it lowercases internally).
118	- **LibreOffice cold start** — the first legacy-format conversion spins up a headless soffice profile (~1–2 s); previews of `.doc/.xls/.ppt` are slower than modern formats.
119	- **PATH in yazi previews** — `piper` runs the command via `sh`; `view-office` must be on the `PATH` yazi inherited. Launch yazi from a configured shell so `~/.dotfiles/bin` is present.
120	
121	## See also
122	
123	- [Data Viewers](../shells/aliases.md) — VisiData wrappers.
124	- [Web reader](web-reader.md) — read HTML pages as markdown (the pandoc/`glow` sibling).
125	- [tool-managers.md](../this_repo/tool-managers.md) — install-side index (doxx, markitdown, libreoffice, `ya pkg`).
126
```

32	#   loaders/_pandas.py auto-registers open_feather → PandasSheet
33	#     → pd.read_feather() → PandasSheet.reload() → dtype_to_type(Series)
34	#     → np.issubdtype(StringDtype, np.integer)  ← ValueError
35	#
36	# This is unavoidable when the .feather schema metadata embeds
37	# `numpy_type: string` (i.e. any DataFrame written from pandas ≥ 2.0 with
38	# string columns). Downgrading the reader doesn't help — the dtype identity
39	# is in the file, and pd.read_feather faithfully restores it.
40	#
41	# The fix is to route .feather through VisiData's *other* loader,
42	# loaders/arrow.py (`ArrowSheet`), which is pure pyarrow and never touches
43	# pandas. Feather v2 IS the Arrow IPC file format, so the same bytes load
44	# cleanly there.
45	#
46	# Implementation note: `setattr(VisiData, 'open_feather', …)` direct
47	# assignment, NOT the `@VisiData.api` decorator. The decorator routes
48	# through the live `vd` instance and (on v3.3) does NOT shadow the class
49	# attribute that loaders/_pandas.py installs at import time, so the
50	# PandasSheet path still wins. Direct class-attribute assignment replaces
51	# the attribute where the loader dispatch looks it up.
52	#
53	# Trade-off: ArrowSheet lacks PandasSheet's vectorized selectByRegex /
54	# in-place sort / undoable addRow/delete_row paths. Everyday "open & look"
55	# is identical; if you specifically want PandasSheet semantics on a
56	# known-StringDtype-free file, fall back to `visidata -f feather <file>`.
57	#

60	# disproves the downgrade path, the upstream code references).
61	# Drop this override once VisiData ships a fix.
62	
63	try:
64	    from visidata import VisiData  # noqa: E402
65	
66	    from visidata.loaders.arrow import ArrowSheet  # noqa: E402
67	
68	    def open_feather(vd, p):  # noqa: ARG001 (signature matches VisiData's contract)
69	        """Route .feather to ArrowSheet (pure pyarrow), bypassing PandasSheet.
70	
71	        Workaround for VisiData 3.3 + pandas StringDtype incompatibility.
72	        See pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md.
73	        """
74	        return ArrowSheet(p.base_stem, source=p)
75	
76	    VisiData.open_feather = open_feather
77	{{- if .enableVimMode }}

91	    # --- INSERT mnemonic ----------------------------------------------------
92	    # `i` -> edit-cell (additive — `e` keeps working as the historical bind).
93	    # Displaces `addcol-incr` (features/incr.py:27).  Still reachable via the
94	    # Alt+H command menu or `Space addcol-incr<Enter>`; the gi / zi / gzi
95	    # set-incr family is unaffected.
96	    TableSheet.unbindkey('i')
97	    TableSheet.bindkey('i', 'edit-cell')
98	
99	    # --- Column navigation (vim line-internal chars) ------------------------
100	    # `0` was unbound by default — free slot, zero trade-off.
101	    # `$` / `_` / `^` displace useful single-letter commands; we relocate
102	    # them to mnemonic 2-char slots in the same block so they're not lost.
103	    #
104	    #   key  | new action       | displaced from   | relocated to
105	    #   -----+------------------+------------------+--------------
106	    #    0   | go-leftmost      | (was unbound)    | -
107	    #    $   | go-rightmost     | type-currency    | z$  (extends $)
108	    #    _   | go-leftmost      | resize-col-max   | zw  (z + Width)
109	    #    ^   | go-leftmost      | rename-col       | zN  (z + Name)
110	    #
111	    # `gh` / `gl` (VisiData defaults) remain bound to go-leftmost/go-rightmost
112	    # and provide a non-overloaded fallback.
113	    TableSheet.bindkey('0', 'go-leftmost')
114	    TableSheet.unbindkey('$'); TableSheet.bindkey('$', 'go-rightmost')
115	    TableSheet.unbindkey('_'); TableSheet.bindkey('_', 'go-leftmost')
116	    TableSheet.unbindkey('^'); TableSheet.bindkey('^', 'go-leftmost')
117	
118	    # Relocate displaced commands to mnemonic 2-char slots.  These slots
119	    # are verified free (no clash with VisiData's existing z*/g* families
120	    # like z_ = resize-col-input, z^ = rename-col-selected, etc.).
121	    TableSheet.bindkey('z$', 'type-currency')
122	    TableSheet.bindkey('zw', 'resize-col-max')
123	    TableSheet.bindkey('zN', 'rename-col')

854	### 15. ya pkg (Yazi plugins)
855	
856	Yazi's built-in plugin manager. `ya` (the yazi CLI companion) clones a plugin, copies it into `~/.config/yazi/plugins/`, and pins its revision in `~/.config/yazi/package.toml`.
857	
858	In this repo the **lockfile is chezmoi-managed** (`dot_config/yazi/package.toml`) and plugins are materialized by a hash-gated run-script, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl`, which runs `ya pkg install` whenever the lockfile changes. `ya pkg install` reads but never rewrites `package.toml`, so there's no chezmoi drift.
859	
860	| Plugin | Purpose |
861	|---|---|
862	| `yazi-rs/plugins:piper` (`piper.yazi`) | "pipe any shell command as a previewer" — backs the Office-document previewers in `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` (`piper -- view-office --preview …`). See [office-viewers.md](../tools/office-viewers.md). |
863	
864	**Add a plugin:** `ya pkg add <owner>/<repo>:<plugin>`, then copy `~/.config/yazi/package.toml` back into the source. **Upgrade:** `ya pkg upgrade` → `just upgrade-yazi-plugins` (install-only by design; apply never bumps revs). Requires a recent yazi (`ya pkg` replaced the older `ya pack`).

159	**Dynamic candidates wired up:**
160	
161	- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.
162	- `pqsum -g <GROUP>` — `_pqsum` shells out to `pueue status --json | jq '.groups | keys[]'`.
163	- `mlf` ids (run-id, experiment-id, model-name) — **not** auto-completed (would round-trip MLflow tracking server, possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` for fuzzy id picking instead.
164	- `yth` video ids — **not** auto-completed (opaque 11-char ids; enumerating the whole history on every TAB is wasteful). Use `tv yth` or `yth search <query>` instead.
165	- `wake` host names — `_wake` shells out to `wake --list-names` (reads `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.
166	
167	**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):
168	
169	1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
170	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
171	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
172	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
173	3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
174	4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).
175	
176	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
177	
178	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
179	
180	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
181	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
182	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
183	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
184

# `wylie102/duckdb.yazi` — Install & Wiring Research

Repo: `github.com/wylie102/duckdb.yazi` · License: MIT. A DuckDB-CLI-powered previewer/preloader for tabular and data files.

## 1. Install command & package.toml

- The README literally shows the **older** syntax: `ya pack -a wylie102/duckdb`.
- The **modern equivalent** (Yazi renamed `ya pack` → `ya pkg`) is:
  ```
  ya pkg add wylie102/duckdb
  ```
  Note the reference is `wylie102/duckdb`, NOT `wylie102/duckdb.yazi` — Yazi's convention strips/appends the `.yazi` suffix automatically. Both commands install the identical package.
- It installs a **single plugin** (`duckdb.yazi`), not a bundle/monorepo subdir. There is no `:subdir` syntax here.
- After adding, `~/.config/yazi/package.toml` gains a locked dependency block of the form:
  ```toml
  [[plugin.deps]]
  use  = "wylie102/duckdb"
  rev  = "<commit-sha>"
  hash = "<integrity-hash>"
  ```
  (The docs' generic example is `use = "owner/my-plugin"`, `rev = "0573024"`, `hash = "..."`.) Keep it updated with `ya pkg upgrade`.

## 2. Required `yazi.toml` config (verbatim from README)

It uses `prepend_previewers` with `run = "duckdb"` — this is the **plugin name** (`duckdb.yazi`), NOT a `piper` piped command. It ALSO requires `prepend_preloaders` (used for cache generation), and there is a **separate `{ ... }` entry per extension** (it does NOT self-declare extensions; the user maps each one).

```toml
[plugin]
prepend_previewers = [
    { name = "*.csv", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.tsv", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.json", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.parquet", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.txt", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.db", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.duckdb", run = "duckdb" }
]

prepend_preloaders = [
    { name = "*.csv", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.tsv", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.json", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.parquet", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.txt", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb", multi = false }
]
```

Notes: `prepend_preloaders` covers only 6 extensions (it excludes `*.db` and `*.duckdb` — database files are not pre-cached). There is **no** `prepend_fetchers` requirement. `multi = false` is set on every preloader entry.

It also needs an **`init.lua`** setup call (required to initialize the plugin):
```lua
require("duckdb"):setup()
-- or with options:
require("duckdb"):setup({
    mode = "standard"/"summarized",   -- Default: "summarized"
    cache_size = 1000,                -- Default: 500
    row_id = true/false/"dynamic",    -- Default: false
    minmax_column_width = int,        -- Default: 21
    column_fit_factor = float,        -- Default: 10.0
})
```

## 3. Targeted extensions (user maps each manually)

Default targets per README and the code's `extension_map`: **csv, tsv, txt, json, parquet, xlsx, db, duckdb**.
- The plugin does **NOT** self-declare/auto-register extensions — each must be listed manually in `prepend_previewers` (and, for the tabular ones, `prepend_preloaders`).
- `.txt` is included only because some tabular files are misnamed `.txt`; the README notes you can omit it if you never need raw-text-as-table.
- `.sqlite` is **NOT** supported (not in the map). `.db` is handled **only if it is an actual DuckDB database** — see #3/#8 caveat below.

## 4. Dependencies (DuckDB CLI + extensions)

- Requires the **`duckdb` CLI binary on PATH**. The README links to DuckDB's install page but does **not state an explicit minimum version number**, and `main.lua` contains **no version check**. Practically, use a recent DuckDB 1.x (the summarize/highlight/`-readonly` behaviors it relies on assume a modern 1.x release).
- Runtime extension usage found in `main.lua`:
  - `install spatial` + `load spatial` — used for **xlsx** reading via `st_read(...)` (chosen over the `excel` extension for more consistent type inference).
  - Core readers `read_csv(...)`, `read_parquet` / `parquet_metadata(...)`, `read_json`, and `SUMMARIZE FROM ...` are built-in to DuckDB.
- **First-run network**: because it runs `INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial`, the **first xlsx preview needs internet** to download the spatial extension from DuckDB's repo (unless already installed/cached in `~/.duckdb`). CSV/TSV/JSON/Parquet/DB previews use built-ins and need **no** network.
- No `sqlite_scanner` / `sqlite` / `excel` extension is installed or loaded anywhere in the code.

## 5. Feather / Arrow (`.feather` / `.arrow`)

**No.** Neither the README nor `main.lua` mentions feather or arrow at all, and they are not in the extension map. DuckDB has no native feather reader, and this plugin does not add one. Not supported.

## 6. Keybindings & features

Bindings are **NOT** shipped in a plugin-owned keymap — the user must add them to their own `keymap.toml` (README-provided block):

```toml
[[manager.prepend_keymap]]
on = "H"
run = "plugin duckdb -1"
desc = "Scroll one column to the left"

[[manager.prepend_keymap]]
on = "L"
run = "plugin duckdb +1"
desc = "Scroll one column to the right"

[[manager.prepend_keymap]]
on = ["g", "o"]
run = "plugin duckdb -open"
desc = "open with duckdb"

[[manager.prepend_keymap]]
on = ["g", "u"]
run = "plugin duckdb -ui"
desc = "open with duckdb ui"
```

Feature notes:
- **Summarized view (SUMMARIZE):** two modes, `standard` and `summarized` (uses DuckDB `SUMMARIZE FROM`). Default mode is set in `init.lua` (`mode = "summarized"` is the plugin default). **Toggle at runtime by pressing `K` while at the top of the file** (this is built into the preview scroll handling, not a separate keymap entry). Vertical row scroll uses `J`/`K`; horizontal **column scroll uses the user-defined `H`/`L`** mapped to `plugin duckdb -1` / `+1`.
- **Row limiting / caching:** on first load it generates Parquet caches for both views (`COPY (...) TO '<cache>' (FORMAT 'parquet')`) to speed scrolling. Standard mode caches `cache_size` rows (default **500**, code: `limit = opts.cache_size or 500`); pagination via `LIMIT %d OFFSET %d`. Other constants: `OFFSET_BASE = 50`, `visible_column_count = 10`, `column_fit_factor = 10`, `minmax_column_width = 21`, internal `cache_version = 3` (baked into `job.skip = 1000000 + cache_version`). README warns that entering a fresh directory triggers cache builds (progress shown bottom-right) during which summarized mode is slower.
- **`g o`** opens the file in the DuckDB CLI; **`g u`** opens the DuckDB UI. Database files (`.db`/`.duckdb`) preview as a table listing (row/column/index counts, PK presence) via `duckdb_tables()` / `duckdb_columns()`, opened read-only (`-readonly`).
- Output highlighting passes through DuckDB's own colors, customizable in `~/.duckdbrc` (e.g. `.highlight_colors column_name magenta bold`, or `.highlight_results off`).

## 7. Conflicts / ordering (e.g. existing `*.xlsx` → `piper -- view-office`)

- `prepend_previewers` **prepends** these rules to the front of Yazi's previewer list. Yazi uses the **first matching** rule, so a prepended `{ name = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb" }` will **win over** any later/user `*.xlsx` mapping (including a `piper -- view-office` entry) and over Yazi defaults.
- Therefore duckdb.yazi effectively **expects to own xlsx** (and the other listed extensions) once you paste its block. If you want `piper -- view-office` to keep xlsx, **remove the `*.xlsx` line** from duckdb's `prepend_previewers`/`prepend_preloaders`, or use `append_previewers` instead of `prepend_` for one of them so ordering favors the other. Two conflicting `prepend_` entries would resolve by their order within the prepended list (first wins).

## 8. Cross-platform

- No OS-specific install steps — it **just needs the `duckdb` binary on PATH** (macOS and Linux both fine; Windows generally works where DuckDB does).
- README explicitly states highlighting "should now work across any os (where duckdb supports it)," i.e. earlier color issues were resolved; colors depend on your terminal + DuckDB build and are tunable in `~/.duckdbrc`.
- One practical macOS/Linux caveat: the **first xlsx preview downloads the `spatial` extension** (network + write to `~/.duckdb`), so behind a firewall/offline you'd want to pre-run `INSTALL spatial;` once. `.db` support assumes a genuine DuckDB database file — a raw SQLite `.db` will not introspect correctly since the plugin uses `duckdb_tables()` and never loads `sqlite_scanner`.

---

### Key caveats to flag
- README's printed install command is the **legacy** `ya pack -a wylie102/duckdb`; use `ya pkg add wylie102/duckdb` on current Yazi.
- **No pinned minimum DuckDB version** is documented — verify against a recent 1.x yourself.
- **xlsx first-run needs internet** (spatial extension); **.sqlite unsupported**, **.db only if truly DuckDB-format**; **feather/arrow unsupported**.
- Keymap bindings and the `init.lua` setup call are **user-supplied**, not auto-installed by `ya pkg add`.

Relevant source references: README at `raw.githubusercontent.com/wylie102/duckdb.yazi/main/README.md` and `main.lua` at `raw.githubusercontent.com/wylie102/duckdb.yazi/main/main.lua`; Yazi CLI docs at `yazi-rs.github.io/docs/cli/`.

# Route A — Add `duckdb.yazi` data-file previewer to yazi

## Context

Yazi currently previews only Office files (`.docx/.xlsx/.pptx` + legacy/OpenDocument) via the
`piper.yazi` → `view-office` pipeline. Data files (`.csv/.tsv/.parquet/.feather/.db/.sqlite`) get no
table preview — they show as raw text or binary/hex on hover.

We evaluated using **visidata** as the previewer and rejected it: visidata's non-interactive `-b`
output is raw TSV (or a `TypeError`-broken `.md`), it can't preview SQLite data (only lists tables),
can't open `.xlsx` (its venv lacks `openpyxl`), and is slow on the hot-path (~0.4s CSV, up to ~10s
cold for parquet). visidata stays the **interactive** opener. For **previews**, `duckdb -box` is far
better (native aligned table, ~0.12s, `LIMIT` for cheap first-N-rows), and a ready-made yazi plugin
already wraps it: **`wylie102/duckdb.yazi`**. Both `duckdb` CLI (devtools role) and `visidata` +
`piper.yazi` are already required in this repo, so this adds **zero new install burden**.

Verified on this host (duckdb 1.4.4, vd 3.3): duckdb renders csv/parquet cleanly and — importantly —
**auto-attaches raw SQLite** `.db` files (`duckdb -readonly t.db` returns both table list and row
data), so duckdb.yazi's `.db` handler covers SQLite despite the plugin source not loading
`sqlite_scanner` explicitly. duckdb has **no feather/arrow reader** (confirmed: `read_parquet`
rejects Arrow IPC, `nanoarrow` ext 404s), so feather is handled by a visidata fallback.

### Decisions (from user)
- **xlsx → duckdb.yazi** (moves off the view-office/markitdown previewer path). First xlsx preview per
  machine downloads DuckDB's `spatial` extension (one-time network) — accepted.
- **Feather/arrow → visidata fallback** via `piper` running `vd -b … --save-filetype fixed` (the one
  clean headless visidata mode; verified renders feather correctly).
- **Keybindings → take the plugin's `H`/`L` + `g o`/`g u` as-is** (overrides yazi's default H/L
  directory-history nav, by explicit choice).

## Changes (file by file)

### 1. `dot_config/yazi/package.toml` — pin the plugin (SSOT, drives install)
Do **not** hand-write `rev`/`hash`. On a live box:
\```
ya pkg add wylie102/duckdb
cp ~/.config/yazi/package.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/yazi/package.toml)"
\```
Adds a second `[[plugin.deps]]` (`use = "wylie102/duckdb"`, `rev`, `hash`) before `[flavor]`. The
hash-gated installer `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` re-runs
`ya pkg install` automatically on the changed sha256 — **no edit to the run-script**. Upgrade path
(`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_yazi_plugins` + `just upgrade-yazi-plugins`) is generic — **no edit**.

### 2. `dot_config/yazi/init.lua` — **NEW FILE** (required; none exists today)
\```lua
-- Initialize the duckdb.yazi data-file previewer.
require("duckdb"):setup({ mode = "standard" })  -- show data rows by default; press K for SUMMARIZE
\```
Without this call the plugin never registers. `mode = "standard"` chosen so hover shows actual rows
(plugin default is `summarized`); one-line change if we prefer summaries.

### 3. `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` — previewer + preloader wiring (lines ~191-205)
- In the existing Office `prepend_previewers`, **remove the `*.xlsx` line** (xlsx now owned by duckdb).
  Keep `*.xls`/`*.ods` on view-office (legacy binary/ODF → LibreOffice; duckdb can't read those).
- **Add duckdb entries** (plugin previewer → `run = "duckdb"`, bare plugin name, not piper):
  `*.csv *.tsv *.parquet *.xlsx *.db *.duckdb *.sqlite *.sqlite3`
- **Add feather/arrow fallback** via piper → visidata `fixed`:
  \```
  { url = "*.feather", run = 'piper -- sh -c ''vd -b "$1" -o - --save-filetype fixed 2>/dev/null | head -n 500'' -- "$1"' },
  { url = "*.arrow",   run = 'piper -- sh -c ''vd -b "$1" -o - --save-filetype fixed 2>/dev/null | head -n 500'' -- "$1"' },
  \```
  (Inline `sh -c` matches the file's existing `sh -lc` opener style; `-- "$1"` passes the path as the
  inner shell's `$1`. `piper.yazi` already installed.)
- **Add `prepend_preloaders`** (duckdb.yazi needs these to build its scroll caches):
  `*.csv *.tsv *.parquet *.xlsx` each `{ … run = "duckdb", multi = false }`.
- Deliberately **omit `*.json` and `*.txt`** from the duckdb map (plugin lists them, but routing all
  JSON/text to a table view would hijack config/log previews).
- **Key-name caveat to verify:** existing Office entries use `url = "*.ext"`; the duckdb.yazi README
  uses `name = "*.ext"`. Mirror the repo's `url =` for consistency, then verify previews actually fire
  (see Verification). If `url` turns out invalid for previewer rules in the installed yazi, that's a
  pre-existing Office-previewer bug — switch the whole `[plugin]` block to `name =` in one pass.

### 4. `dot_config/yazi/keymap.toml` — plugin keybindings (currently all-commented template)
Add a `[manager] prepend_keymap` with the 4 documented binds verbatim:
`H` → `plugin duckdb -1`, `L` → `plugin duckdb +1` (scroll columns), `g o` → `plugin duckdb -open`
(open in duckdb CLI), `g u` → `plugin duckdb -ui`. Note in a comment that H/L override yazi's default
directory-history nav (chosen deliberately). SUMMARIZE toggle is `K` at top-of-file — built into the
plugin, no keymap entry needed.

### 5. Docs (CLAUDE.md cross-file rules mandate same-commit updates)
- **NEW `docs/tools/data-viewers.md`** — the duckdb.yazi previewer: formats, `K`/`H`/`L`/`g o`/`g u`,
  the xlsx-spatial-first-run-network note, the feather→visidata fallback, SQLite-via-duckdb-auto-attach.
  Cross-link ↔ `office-viewers.md` and `../shells/aliases.md` (visidata).
- **`mkdocs.yml`** — nav entry next to `Office viewers … tools/office-viewers.md` (~line 334):
  `- Data viewers (duckdb.yazi): tools/data-viewers.md`. Then `uv run mkdocs build --strict`.
- **`docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`** — § 15 (`ya pkg`) add a `duckdb.yazi` row under `piper.yazi`;
  A–Z index add a `duckdb.yazi` plugin row (mechanism `ya pkg`, role `devtools (yazi)`). The `duckdb`
  **CLI** row already exists — leave it.
- **`docs/tools/office-viewers.md`** — one line noting `.xlsx` **preview** now routes to duckdb.yazi
  (the `view-office --preview file.xlsx` CLI path via markitdown is unchanged; only yazi's previewer
  moved). markitdown's `[docx,xlsx,pptx]` extras **stay** (CLI still uses them).
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — add a "Data-file viewing" row to the cross-file table (sibling of "Office
  viewing") listing: `package.toml` duckdb dep, `yazi.toml` duckdb entries, **`init.lua`** requirement,
  `keymap.toml` binds, the **feather piper→`vd --save-filetype fixed` contract**, and the
  "xlsx preview owned by duckdb.yazi (needs spatial ext, network-on-first-use)" note.
- **`README.md`** — optional: extend the yazi/duckdb bullet to mention data-file table previews.

## Critical files
- Functional: `dot_config/yazi/package.toml`, `dot_config/yazi/init.lua` (new),
  `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml`, `dot_config/yazi/keymap.toml`
- Reused as-is (no edit): `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl`,
  `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`, `justfile`, `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (duckdb CLI),
  `dot_visidatarc.tmpl` (feather ArrowSheet override already deployed)
- Docs: `docs/tools/data-viewers.md` (new), `mkdocs.yml`, `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`,
  `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`

## Verification (end-to-end)
1. `ya pkg add wylie102/duckdb` on this host; copy `package.toml` back; `chezmoi diff` the yazi files.
2. `chezmoi apply` (or `chezmoi apply ~/.config/yazi`) → confirm `ya pkg install` materializes
   `~/.config/yazi/plugins/duckdb.yazi/`, and `init.lua`/`keymap.toml` deploy.
3. Launch `yazi` and hover each test file (already generated in `/tmp`: `t.csv t.parquet t.feather
   t.db`; make a `t.xlsx`): confirm each renders an aligned table. **This confirms the `url=` vs
   `name=` key question** — if a `.csv` shows a table, the key is correct.

   - `.db`/`.sqlite`: confirm table-listing + that SQLite files preview (duckdb auto-attach).

   - `.xlsx`: confirm duckdb table (first run may pause to fetch `spatial`).

5. `uv run mkdocs build --strict` passes (docs + nav).

## Follow-ups / notes

```text
=== piper.yazi main.lua (how it runs the command + passes file) ===
--- @since 26.1.22

local M = {}

local function fail(job, s) ya.preview_widget(job, ui.Text.parse(s):area(job.area):wrap(ui.Wrap.YES)) end

function M:peek(job)
	local child, err = Command("sh")
		:arg({ "-c", job.args[1], "sh", tostring(job.file.path) })
		:env("w", job.area.w)
		:env("h", job.area.h)
		:env("t", rt.term.light and "light" or "dark")
		:env("CYGWIN", "noupcaseenv")
		:stdout(Command.PIPED)
		:stderr(Command.PIPED)
		:spawn()

	if not child then
		return fail(job, "sh: " .. err)
	end

	local limit = job.area.h
	local i, outs, errs = 0, {}, {}
	repeat
		local next, event = child:read_line()
		if event == 1 then
			errs[#errs + 1] = next
		elseif event ~= 0 then
			break
		end

		i = i + 1
		if i > job.skip then
			outs[#outs + 1] = next
		end
	until i >= job.skip + limit

	child:start_kill()
	if #errs > 0 then
		fail(job, table.concat(errs, ""))
	elseif job.skip > 0 and i < job.skip + limit then
		ya.emit("peek", { math.max(0, i - limit), only_if = job.file.url, upper_bound = true })
	else
		ya.preview_widget(job, M.format(job, outs))
	end
end

function M:seek(job) require("code"):seek(job) end

function M.format(job, lines)
	local format = job.args.format
	if format ~= "url" then
		local s = table.concat(lines, ""):gsub("\t", string.rep(" ", rt.preview.tab_size))
		return ui.Text.parse(s):area(job.area)
	end

	for i = 1, #lines do
		lines[i] = lines[i]:gsub("[\r\n]+$", "")

		local icon
		if th.icon then
			icon = th.icon:match(File {
				url = Url(lines[i]),
				cha = Cha { mode = tonumber(lines[i]:sub(-1) == "/" and "40700" or "100644", 8) },
			})
		else -- TODO: remove
			icon = File({
				url = Url(lines[i]),
				cha = Cha { mode = tonumber(lines[i]:sub(-1) == "/" and "40700" or "100644", 8) },
			}):icon()
		end

		if icon then
			lines[i] = ui.Line { ui.Span(" " .. icon.text .. " "):style(icon.style), lines[i] }
		end
	end
	return ui.Text(lines):area(job.area)
end

return M

=== piper README usage (if present) ===
# piper.yazi

Pipe any shell command as a previewer.

## Installation

```sh
ya pkg add yazi-rs/plugins:piper
```

## Usage

Piper is a general-purpose previewer - you can pass any shell command to `piper` and it will use the command's output as the preview content.

It accepts a string parameter, which is the shell command to be executed, for example:

```toml
# ~/.config/yazi/yazi.toml
[[plugin.prepend_previewers]]
url = "*"
run = 'piper -- echo "$1"'
```

This will set `piper` as the previewer for all file types and use `$1` (file path) as the preview content.

## Variables

Available variables:

- `$1`: path of the file being previewed.
- `$w`: width of the preview area.
- `$h`: height of the preview area.
- `$t`: terminal theme mode, either `"dark"` or `"light"`.

## Examples

Here are some configuration examples:

### Preview tarballs with [`tar`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/tar.1.html)

# ~/.config/yazi/keymap.toml
# Yazi keybindings customization. Managed by chezmoi
# (source: dot_config/yazi/keymap.toml).

# --- duckdb.yazi previewer keybindings ---
# Companion to the data-file previewers in yazi.toml [plugin] and the required
# `require("duckdb"):setup{}` in init.lua. See docs/tools/data-viewers.md.
#
# ⚠ H / L OVERRIDE Yazi's default history back/forward (the capital-letter binds).
#   Lowercase h / l (leave / enter directory) are UNAFFECTED. While previewing a
#   data file, H / L scroll the visible columns; on other files they no-op.
#   The SUMMARIZE ⇄ standard view toggle is `K` at top-of-file — built into the
#   plugin, so it needs no keymap entry here.
[mgr]

  { on = "L", run = "plugin duckdb +1", desc = "DuckDB preview: scroll one column right" },
  { on = [ "g", "o" ], run = "plugin duckdb -open", desc = "Open file in the DuckDB CLI" },
  { on = [ "g", "u" ], run = "plugin duckdb -ui", desc = "Open file in the DuckDB UI" },
]

```md
# View Data Files in the Terminal

Preview and explore tabular / data files — **CSV**, **TSV**, **Parquet**, **Feather/Arrow**,
**Excel `.xlsx`**, **SQLite**, and native **DuckDB** databases — without leaving the terminal, and
without opening an editor or a GUI.

Two layers:

- **Inline previews** in the [yazi](tmux/README.md) file manager — hover a data file and its rows
  render as an aligned table in the right pane, powered by the [`duckdb.yazi`](#duckdbyazi--the-previewer)
  plugin (with two small fallbacks for the formats DuckDB can't read).
- **Interactive exploration** with [VisiData](#visidata--interactive-exploration) (`vd`) — a fast,
  vim-keyed spreadsheet TUI for sorting, filtering, frequency tables, and describe.

The split is deliberate: **DuckDB for the glance, VisiData for the deep-dive.** We evaluated using
VisiData for previews too and rejected it — its non-interactive batch output is raw TSV (or a
`--save-filetype fixed` monochrome table), it can't preview SQLite data (only lists tables), can't
open `.xlsx` (its tool venv has no `openpyxl`), and is slow on the preview hot-path (~0.4 s for CSV,
up to ~10 s cold for parquet, because it imports pandas + pyarrow). DuckDB's `-box` renders a native
aligned table in ~0.1 s and can cheaply `LIMIT` to the first N rows.

## TL;DR

| Format | yazi preview | Engine |
|---|---|---|
| `.csv` `.tsv` | ✅ table | duckdb.yazi |
| `.parquet` | ✅ table | duckdb.yazi |
| `.xlsx` | ✅ table | duckdb.yazi (DuckDB `spatial` ext — see gotcha) |
| `.db` `.duckdb` | ✅ table listing | duckdb.yazi (DuckDB auto-attaches SQLite) |
| `.sqlite` `.sqlite3` | ✅ table listing | piper → `duckdb -readonly` (fallback) |
| `.feather` `.arrow` | ✅ table | piper → VisiData `fixed` (DuckDB has no Arrow-IPC reader) |

All formats open interactively in **VisiData** (`vd <file>`) regardless of the preview engine.

## `duckdb.yazi` — the previewer

[`duckdb.yazi`](https://github.com/wylie102/duckdb.yazi) is a Yazi previewer/preloader plugin that
shells out to the **`duckdb` CLI** (already installed by the `devtools` role) and renders its `-box`
table into the preview pane. It reads CSV, TSV, Parquet, Excel, and DuckDB/SQLite databases.

Three pieces make it work in this repo:

| Piece | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Lockfile (SSOT) | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml` | pins `wylie102/duckdb` (rev + hash) |
| Init | `dot_config/yazi/init.lua` | **required** `require("duckdb"):setup({ mode = "standard" })` |
| Wiring | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin]` | `prepend_previewers` + `prepend_preloaders` (`run = "duckdb"`) |

The `setup()` call in `init.lua` is mandatory — without it the `run = "duckdb"` rules never activate.
We set `mode = "standard"` so hover shows actual data rows (the plugin default is `summarized`); press
`K` at the top of a preview to toggle to DuckDB's `SUMMARIZE` view (min/max/counts per column).

### Keybindings

Added to `dot_config/yazi/keymap.toml` (`[mgr] prepend_keymap`):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `K` | Toggle standard ⇄ SUMMARIZE view (built into the plugin; no keymap entry) |
| `H` / `L` | Scroll one column left / right in the preview |
| `g o` | Open the hovered file in the DuckDB CLI |
| `g u` | Open the hovered file in the DuckDB UI |

> ⚠ **`H` / `L` override Yazi's default history back/forward** (the capital-letter binds). Lowercase
> `h` / `l` (leave / enter directory) are unaffected. On non-data files `H`/`L` no-op.

### The two fallbacks (formats DuckDB can't read)

- **Feather / Arrow** (`.feather` `.arrow`) — DuckDB has no Arrow-IPC file reader, so these route
  through [`piper.yazi`](office-viewers.md#the-ya-pkg-plugin-mechanism) to VisiData's non-interactive
  `fixed` saver:
  \```toml
  { url = "*.feather", run = 'piper -- vd -b -f arrow "$1" -o - --save-filetype fixed 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' }
  \```
  `-f arrow` forces the pure-pyarrow `ArrowSheet` loader (dodges the pandas `StringDtype` crash — see
  [the feather pitfall](../../pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md)), and `2>/dev/null`
  is **mandatory**: piper renders any stderr as an error preview, and VisiData logs status to stderr.
- **SQLite by `.sqlite` / `.sqlite3` name** — the plugin's internal `extension_map` only knows `.db`
  (not `.sqlite`), so those two extensions route through piper to a `duckdb -readonly` table listing.
  Plain `.db` gets the full plugin treatment (DuckDB transparently attaches SQLite databases opened
  directly, so `.db` covers most SQLite files).

## VisiData — interactive exploration

`vd <file>` opens a full-screen, vim-keyed spreadsheet over CSV/TSV/JSON/Parquet/Feather/Arrow/xlsx/
SQLite. This is the tool for actual analysis: sort, filter (`|` / `\`), frequency (`Shift+F`),
describe (`Shift+I`), pivot, and save-as. Defaults are already vim-flavored (`h/j/k/l`, `gg/G`,
`/?` search); the repo adds strict-vim column nav under `enableVimMode`. See
[aliases.md → Data Viewers](../shells/aliases.md#data-viewers) for the `vd-arrow` / `vd-ro` wrappers
and [vim-mode.md → VisiData](../this_repo/vim-mode.md#visidata) for the key rebinds.

VisiData and its companion `~/.visidatarc` are installed/managed regardless (`visidata` is a required
uv tool with `pandas` + `pyarrow`); the `.visidatarc` carries the `.feather` → `ArrowSheet` reroute
that the preview fallback above also relies on.

## Where things live

| Surface | Path |
|---|---|
| Plugin lockfile + installer | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` |
| Plugin init | `dot_config/yazi/init.lua` |
| Previewers + preloaders | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin]` |
| Keybindings | `dot_config/yazi/keymap.toml` |
| DuckDB CLI install | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
| VisiData install + rc | `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`, `dot_visidatarc.tmpl` |
| Upgrades | `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`) |

## Gotchas

- **`.xlsx` first preview needs internet.** duckdb.yazi reads Excel via DuckDB's `spatial` extension,
  which it `INSTALL`s on first use — the first `.xlsx` preview on a fresh machine downloads it (cached
  in `~/.duckdb` afterwards). CSV/TSV/Parquet/DB previews use built-ins and need no network.
- **`.xlsx` preview moved off `view-office`.** Yazi now previews `.xlsx` with duckdb.yazi, not
  `markitdown`. The `view-office --preview budget.xlsx` **CLI** is unchanged (still markitdown → glow);
  only Yazi's previewer wiring moved. See [office-viewers.md](office-viewers.md).
- **Lowercase globs.** The `url` globs are lowercase (`*.csv`); a file named `DATA.CSV` won't trigger
  the previewer. (VisiData opened directly still works.)
- **DuckDB normalizes display.** `-box` may render `1200.50` as `1200.5` (type inference) — it's a
  display artifact of the preview, not a change to the file.
- **`view-office` for `.xls`/`.ods`.** Legacy binary `.xls` and OpenDocument `.ods` stay on the
  LibreOffice → OOXML path (DuckDB can't read those); only modern `.xlsx` uses duckdb.yazi.

## See also

- [Office viewers](office-viewers.md) — the `.docx/.pptx` + legacy/ODF sibling stack (doxx / markitdown / LibreOffice), and the `ya pkg` / `piper.yazi` mechanism shared here.
- [Data Viewers (aliases)](../shells/aliases.md#data-viewers) — VisiData `vd-arrow` / `vd-ro` wrappers.
- [tool-managers.md § 15](../this_repo/tool-managers.md) — `ya pkg` plugin mechanism (piper.yazi, duckdb.yazi).
- [Feather / StringDtype pitfall](../../pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md) — why `.feather` needs the ArrowSheet loader.

443	# --- bat ---
444	- name: Install bat (Debian/Ubuntu)

446	  become: true
447	  tags: [sudo]
448	  ansible.builtin.apt:
449	    name: bat
450	    state: present
451	
452	- name: Create bat symlink on Debian/Ubuntu
453	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
454	  become: true
455	  tags: [sudo]
456	  ansible.builtin.file:
457	    src: /usr/bin/batcat
458	    dest: /usr/bin/bat
459	    state: link
460	  ignore_errors: true
461	
462	- name: Detect Linuxbrew for bat (Debian/Ubuntu)
463	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
464	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v brew || true
465	  args:
466	    executable: /bin/bash

470	- name: Install bat via Linuxbrew when available (Debian/Ubuntu)
471	  when:

473	    - bat_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''
474	  community.general.homebrew:
475	    name: bat
476	    state: present

479	# Gate broadened to RedHat per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md — bat ships
480	# `-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` and works on glibc 2.17.
481	- name: Re-check if bat is installed
482	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
483	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v bat
484	  register: bat_recheck
485	  changed_when: false
486	  failed_when: false
487	
488	- name: Install bat from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
489	  when:
490	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
491	    - bat_recheck.rc != 0
492	  block:
493	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (bat)
494	      ansible.builtin.file:
495	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
496	        state: directory
497	        mode: '0755'
498	
499	    - name: Get latest bat release
500	      ansible.builtin.uri:
501	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/sharkdp/bat/releases/latest
502	        return_content: true
503	      register: bat_release
504	
505	    - name: Download bat binary
506	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
507	        url: "https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/releases/download/{{ bat_release.json.tag_name }}/bat-{{ bat_release.json.tag_name }}-{{ target_architecture }}-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
508	        dest: /tmp/bat.tar.gz
509	        mode: '0644'
510	        timeout: 120
511	      retries: 3
512	      delay: 5
513	
514	    - name: Extract bat
515	      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
516	        src: /tmp/bat.tar.gz
517	        dest: /tmp
518	        remote_src: true
519	
520	    - name: Install bat to ~/.local/bin
521	      ansible.builtin.copy:
522	        src: "/tmp/bat-{{ bat_release.json.tag_name }}-{{ target_architecture }}-unknown-linux-musl/bat"
523	        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/bat"
524	        mode: '0755'
525	        remote_src: true
526	
527	    - name: Clean up bat temp files
528	      ansible.builtin.file:
529	        path: "{{ item }}"
530	        state: absent
531	      loop:
532	        - /tmp/bat.tar.gz
533	        - "/tmp/bat-{{ bat_release.json.tag_name }}-{{ target_architecture }}-unknown-linux-musl"
534	
535	  rescue:
536	    - name: Warn bat installation failed
537	      ansible.builtin.debug:
538	        msg: "bat installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
539	
540	    - name: Clean up bat temp files after failure
541	      ansible.builtin.file:
542	        path: "{{ item }}"
543	        state: absent
544	      loop:
545	        - /tmp/bat.tar.gz

547	# --- bats (bats-core: Bash test runner) ---
548	- name: Install bats (Debian/Ubuntu)

553	    name: bats

556	# --- bats (user-level fallback) ---
557	# Gate broadened to RedHat per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md — the user-level
558	# install (curl GitHub release tarball, run install.sh) has no apt-specific
559	# behaviour and works on any glibc-2.17+ system.
560	- name: Re-check if bats is installed
561	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
562	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v bats

569	- name: Install bats-core from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
570	  when:

572	    - bats_recheck.rc != 0
573	  block:
574	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (bats)
575	      ansible.builtin.file:
576	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
577	        state: directory

581	      ansible.builtin.uri:

583	        return_content: true
584	      register: bats_release
585	
586	    - name: Download bats-core tarball
587	      ansible.builtin.get_url:

589	        dest: /tmp/bats.tar.gz
590	        mode: '0644'
591	        timeout: 120
592	      retries: 3
593	      delay: 5
594	
595	    - name: Extract and install bats-core to ~/.local
596	      ansible.builtin.shell: |

598	        rm -rf /tmp/bats-extract
599	        mkdir -p /tmp/bats-extract
600	        tar -xzf /tmp/bats.tar.gz -C /tmp/bats-extract --strip-components=1
601	        /tmp/bats-extract/install.sh "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local"
602	      args:

606	    - name: Clean up bats temp files

609	        state: absent

612	        - /tmp/bats-extract

620	      ansible.builtin.file:
621	        path: "{{ item }}"
622	        state: absent
623	      loop:
624	        - /tmp/bats.tar.gz
625	        - /tmp/bats-extract

627	# --- zoxide ---
628	- name: Check if zoxide is installed
629	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
630	  ansible.builtin.command: zoxide --version
631	  register: zoxide_check
632	  changed_when: false
633	  failed_when: false
634	
635	- name: Install zoxide via official installer (Debian/Ubuntu)
636	  when:
637	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
638	    - zoxide_check.rc != 0
639	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
640	    curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide/main/install.sh | sh
641	  args:
642	    creates: "{{ ansible_facts.env.HOME }}/.local/bin/zoxide"
643	  failed_when: false
644	  register: zoxide_install_result
645	
646	- name: Warn zoxide installation failed
647	  when:
648	    - zoxide_install_result is defined
649	    - zoxide_install_result.rc is defined
650	    - zoxide_install_result.rc != 0
651	  ansible.builtin.debug:
652	    msg: "zoxide installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
653	
654	# --- eza ---
655	- name: Check if eza is installed
656	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
657	  ansible.builtin.command: eza --version
658	  register: eza_check
659	  changed_when: false
660	  failed_when: false
661	
662	- name: Install eza via official installer (Debian/Ubuntu)
663	  when:
664	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
665	    - eza_check.rc != 0
666	  become: true
667	  tags: [sudo]
668	  block:
669	    - name: Add eza GPG key
670	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
671	        mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
672	        wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eza-community/eza/main/deb.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/gierens.gpg
673	      args:
674	        creates: /etc/apt/keyrings/gierens.gpg
675	
676	    # deb822_repository (apt_repository is deprecated, removed in
677	    # ansible-core 2.25) writes the .sources file WITHOUT running
678	    # `apt update`, so we verify reachability ourselves and roll the file
679	    # back when the repo is broken/unreachable (GFW hosts) — a leftover
680	    # broken source would otherwise fail the base role's cache update on
681	    # every subsequent run. The GitHub-release fallback below installs eza
682	    # in that case. Requires python3-debian (installed by the base role).
683	    - name: Remove legacy one-line eza source (pre-deb822 format)
684	      ansible.builtin.file:
685	        path: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/gierens.list
686	        state: absent
687	
688	    - name: Add eza repository (deb822)
689	      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
690	        name: gierens
691	        types: deb
692	        uris: http://deb.gierens.de
693	        suites: stable
694	        components: main
695	        signed_by: /etc/apt/keyrings/gierens.gpg
696	      ignore_errors: true
697	      register: eza_repo
698	
699	    - name: Refresh apt cache (eza repo)
700	      when: eza_repo is succeeded
701	      ansible.builtin.apt:
702	        update_cache: true
703	      ignore_errors: true
704	
705	    # The apt module treats a partially-failed `apt update` (one unreachable
706	    # source, others fine) as SUCCESS-with-warnings, so its failed/succeeded
707	    # status can't tell us whether the gierens repo actually works. Probe
708	    # deterministically: eza resolvable from deb.gierens.de ⇒ keep + install;
709	    # otherwise roll the .sources file back so it can't slow down / break
710	    # later apt updates, and let the GitHub fallback below take over.
711	    - name: Check eza is resolvable from the gierens repo
712	      when: eza_repo is succeeded
713	      ansible.builtin.command: apt-cache policy eza
714	      register: eza_policy
715	      changed_when: false
716	      failed_when: false
717	
718	    - name: Remove eza repository (broken or unreachable)
719	      when:
720	        - eza_repo is succeeded
721	        - "'deb.gierens.de' not in (eza_policy.stdout | default(''))"
722	      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
723	        name: gierens
724	        state: absent
725	
726	    - name: Install eza from repository
727	      ansible.builtin.apt:
728	        name: eza
729	        state: present
730	      when: "'deb.gierens.de' in (eza_policy.stdout | default(''))"
731	      ignore_errors: true
732	  rescue:
733	    - name: Warn eza apt install failed
734	      ansible.builtin.debug:
735	        msg: "eza apt install failed (likely broken third-party repo) — will try GitHub fallback"
736	
737	# --- eza (user-level fallback) ---
738	# Upstream publishes a musl tarball for x86_64 only. aarch64 has just
739	# `unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`, which can break on Jammy when upstream CI uses a
740	# newer glibc. Split the user fallback by arch:
741	#   - x86_64: switch to `eza_x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`.
742	#   - aarch64: probe Linuxbrew; install via brew if present, otherwise skip
743	#     with an explicit warning.
744	- name: Re-check if eza is installed
745	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
746	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v eza
747	  register: eza_recheck
748	  changed_when: false
749	  failed_when: false
750	
751	- name: Install eza musl from GitHub releases (user-level, x86_64)
752	  when:
753	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
754	    - eza_recheck.rc != 0
755	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
756	  block:
757	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (eza)
758	      ansible.builtin.file:
759	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
760	        state: directory
761	        mode: '0755'
762	
763	    - name: Get latest eza release
764	      ansible.builtin.uri:
765	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/eza-community/eza/releases/latest
766	        return_content: true
767	      register: eza_release
768	
769	    - name: Download eza musl binary (x86_64)
770	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
771	        url: "https://github.com/eza-community/eza/releases/download/{{ eza_release.json.tag_name }}/eza_x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
772	        dest: /tmp/eza.tar.gz
773	        mode: '0644'
774	        timeout: 120
775	      retries: 3
776	      delay: 5
777	
778	    - name: Extract eza to ~/.local/bin
779	      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
780	        src: /tmp/eza.tar.gz

805	    - eza_recheck.rc != 0

809	    executable: /bin/bash
810	  register: eza_brew_probe

814	  when:

820	  community.general.homebrew:

827	    - eza_recheck.rc != 0

829	    - (eza_brew_probe is not defined) or (eza_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim == '')
830	  ansible.builtin.debug:

837	# --- git-delta ---
838	# Delta can start successfully but crash when reading stdin if bat's binary
839	# theme cache was built by an incompatible bat version. Verify by actually
840	# feeding delta an empty diff, not only by checking `--version`.
841	# Glibc landscape:
842	#   - x86_64: upstream publishes `unknown-linux-musl` (static, glibc-independent).
843	#     User-level fallback now uses it (was `unknown-linux-gnu` until the
844	#     centos7-noroot.md sweep). Works on glibc 2.17.
845	#   - aarch64: only `unknown-linux-gnu` assets exist, and delta 0.19.x briefly
846	#     required glibc 2.39 (unavailable on Jammy). We therefore:
847	#       1) sudo path (apt .deb) is Debian/Ubuntu-only.
848	#       2) aarch64 falls through to Linuxbrew (`brew install git-delta`) or
849	#          skips with a clear debug message rather than silently pulling a
850	#          glibc-risky binary.
851	- name: Check if delta is installed
852	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
853	  ansible.builtin.shell: printf '' | delta --no-gitconfig --paging=never
854	  args:
855	    executable: /bin/bash
856	  register: delta_check
857	  changed_when: false
858	  failed_when: false
859	
860	- name: Skip git-delta on unsupported architecture
861	  when:
862	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
863	    - delta_check.rc != 0
864	    - target_architecture not in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
865	  ansible.builtin.debug:
866	    msg: "git-delta skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"
867	
868	- name: Install git-delta .deb (Debian/Ubuntu, x86_64)
869	  when:
870	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
871	    - delta_check.rc != 0
872	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
873	  become: true
874	  tags: [sudo]
875	  block:
876	    - name: Get latest delta release
877	      ansible.builtin.uri:
878	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/dandavison/delta/releases/latest
879	        return_content: true
880	      register: delta_release
881	
882	    - name: Download git-delta .deb package
883	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
884	        url: "https://github.com/dandavison/delta/releases/download/{{ delta_release.json.tag_name }}/git-delta_{{ delta_release.json.tag_name }}_amd64.deb"
885	        dest: /tmp/git-delta.deb
886	        mode: '0644'
887	        timeout: 120
888	      retries: 3
889	      delay: 5
890	
891	    - name: Install delta .deb package
892	      ansible.builtin.apt:
893	        deb: /tmp/git-delta.deb
894	
895	    - name: Clean up delta .deb
896	      ansible.builtin.file:
897	        path: /tmp/git-delta.deb
898	        state: absent
899	
900	  rescue:
901	    - name: Warn git-delta installation failed
902	      ansible.builtin.debug:
903	        msg: "git-delta installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
904	
905	    - name: Clean up git-delta temp files after failure
906	      ansible.builtin.file:
907	        path: /tmp/git-delta.deb
908	        state: absent
909	
910	# --- git-delta (aarch64: brew or skip — no upstream musl asset) ---
911	- name: Detect Linuxbrew for git-delta (Debian/Ubuntu, aarch64)
912	  when:
913	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
914	    - delta_check.rc != 0
915	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
916	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v brew || true
917	  args:
918	    executable: /bin/bash
919	  register: delta_brew_probe
920	  changed_when: false
921	
922	- name: Install git-delta via Linuxbrew (Debian/Ubuntu, aarch64, brew available)
923	  when:
924	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
925	    - delta_check.rc != 0
926	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
927	    - delta_brew_probe is defined
928	    - delta_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''
929	  community.general.homebrew:
930	    name: git-delta
931	    state: present
932	
933	- name: Warn git-delta cannot be installed safely (aarch64, no brew)
934	  when:
935	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
936	    - delta_check.rc != 0
937	    - target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
938	    - (delta_brew_probe is not defined) or (delta_brew_probe.stdout | default('') | trim == '')
939	  ansible.builtin.debug:
940	    msg: >-
941	      git-delta skipped on aarch64: upstream publishes only `unknown-linux-gnu`
942	      assets, which historically require glibc >= 2.39 and may fail on Jammy
943	      (glibc 2.35). Install Linuxbrew (`brew install git-delta`) or wait for
944	      an upstream musl arm64 build.
945	
946	# --- git-delta (user-level fallback) ---
947	# Gate broadened to RedHat per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md — x86_64 uses the
948	# upstream `unknown-linux-musl` tarball (glibc-independent). aarch64 still
949	# has no upstream musl; that path stays Debian-only (Linuxbrew aarch64 on
950	# CentOS 7 is not a typical setup we support).
951	- name: Re-check if delta is installed
952	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
953	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v delta && printf '' | delta --no-gitconfig --paging=never
954	  args:
955	    executable: /bin/bash
956	  register: delta_recheck
957	  changed_when: false
958	  failed_when: false
959	
960	- name: Install git-delta tarball (user-level, no sudo, x86_64)
961	  when:
962	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
963	    - delta_recheck.rc != 0
964	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
965	  block:
966	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (delta)
967	      ansible.builtin.file:
968	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
969	        state: directory
970	        mode: '0755'
971	
972	    - name: Get latest delta release (user)
973	      ansible.builtin.uri:
974	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/dandavison/delta/releases/latest
975	        return_content: true
976	      register: delta_release_user
977	
978	    - name: Download delta musl tarball (user)
979	      # Switched from `-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` to the musl variant
980	      # so CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17) can install it without source build. The
981	      # gnu tarball historically required glibc 2.39 on aarch64 too.
982	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
983	        url: "https://github.com/dandavison/delta/releases/download/{{ delta_release_user.json.tag_name }}/delta-{{ delta_release_user.json.tag_name }}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
984	        dest: /tmp/delta.tar.gz
985	        mode: '0644'
986	        timeout: 120
987	      retries: 3
988	      delay: 5
989	
990	    - name: Extract delta (user)
991	      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
992	        src: /tmp/delta.tar.gz
993	        dest: /tmp
994	        remote_src: true
995	
996	    - name: Install delta to ~/.local/bin
997	      ansible.builtin.copy:
998	        src: "/tmp/delta-{{ delta_release_user.json.tag_name }}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/delta"
999	        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/delta"
1000	        mode: '0755'
1001	        remote_src: true
1002	
1003	    - name: Clean up delta temp files (user)
1004	      ansible.builtin.file:
1005	        path: "{{ item }}"
1006	        state: absent
1007	      loop:
1008	        - /tmp/delta.tar.gz
1009	        - "/tmp/delta-{{ delta_release_user.json.tag_name }}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"
1010	
1011	  rescue:
1012	    - name: Warn git-delta (user) installation failed
1013	      ansible.builtin.debug:
1014	        msg: "git-delta (user) installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
1015	
1016	    - name: Clean up git-delta (user) temp files after failure
1017	      ansible.builtin.file:
1018	        path: "{{ item }}"
1019	        state: absent
1020	      loop:
1021	        - /tmp/delta.tar.gz

1058	# --- diffnav ---
1059	- name: Check if diffnav is installed
1060	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1061	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v diffnav
1062	  register: diffnav_check
1063	  changed_when: false
1064	  failed_when: false
1065	  environment:
1066	    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
1067	
1068	- name: Set diffnav release architecture
1069	  # Broadened to RedHat + decoupled from diffnav_check so the user-level
1070	  # fallback works on CentOS 7 where the sudo .deb install is skipped.
1071	  when:
1072	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
1073	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
1074	    diffnav_release_arch: >-
1075	      {{
1076	        'x86_64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
1077	        else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
1078	        else ''
1079	      }}
1080	
1081	- name: Skip diffnav on unsupported architecture
1082	  when:
1083	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1084	    - diffnav_check.rc != 0
1085	    - diffnav_release_arch == ''
1086	  ansible.builtin.debug:
1087	    msg: "diffnav skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"
1088	
1089	- name: Install diffnav from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu)
1090	  when:
1091	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1092	    - diffnav_check.rc != 0
1093	    - diffnav_release_arch != ''
1094	  become: true
1095	  tags: [sudo]
1096	  block:
1097	    - name: Get latest diffnav release
1098	      ansible.builtin.uri:
1099	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/dlvhdr/diffnav/releases/latest
1100	        return_content: true
1101	      register: diffnav_release
1102	
1103	    - name: Download diffnav tarball
1104	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
1105	        url: "https://github.com/dlvhdr/diffnav/releases/download/{{ diffnav_release.json.tag_name }}/diffnav_Linux_{{ diffnav_release_arch }}.tar.gz"
1106	        dest: /tmp/diffnav.tar.gz
1107	        mode: '0644'
1108	        timeout: 120
1109	      retries: 3
1110	      delay: 5
1111	
1112	    - name: Extract and install diffnav
1113	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
1114	        set -euo pipefail
1115	        rm -rf /tmp/diffnav-extract
1116	        mkdir -p /tmp/diffnav-extract
1117	        tar -xzf /tmp/diffnav.tar.gz -C /tmp/diffnav-extract
1118	        diffnav_bin="$(find /tmp/diffnav-extract -type f -name diffnav | head -n 1)"
1119	        install -m 0755 "$diffnav_bin" /usr/local/bin/diffnav
1120	      args:
1121	        executable: /bin/bash
1122	      changed_when: true
1123	
1124	    - name: Clean up diffnav temp files
1125	      ansible.builtin.file:
1126	        path: "{{ item }}"
1127	        state: absent
1128	      loop:
1129	        - /tmp/diffnav.tar.gz
1130	        - /tmp/diffnav-extract
1131	
1132	  rescue:
1133	    - name: Warn diffnav installation failed
1134	      ansible.builtin.debug:
1135	        msg: "diffnav installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
1136	
1137	    - name: Clean up diffnav temp files after failure
1138	      ansible.builtin.file:
1139	        path: "{{ item }}"
1140	        state: absent
1141	      loop:
1142	        - /tmp/diffnav.tar.gz
1143	        - /tmp/diffnav-extract

1339	# --- tldr ---
1340	- name: Check if tldr is installed
1341	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1342	  ansible.builtin.command: tldr --version
1343	  register: tldr_check
1344	  changed_when: false
1345	  failed_when: false
1346	
1347	- name: Check for system npm
1348	  when:
1349	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1350	    - tldr_check.rc != 0
1351	  ansible.builtin.command: command -v npm
1352	  register: system_npm_check
1353	  changed_when: false
1354	  failed_when: false
1355	
1356	- name: Install tldr via npm (Debian/Ubuntu, system-level)
1357	  when:
1358	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1359	    - tldr_check.rc != 0
1360	    - system_npm_check.rc == 0
1361	  become: true
1362	  tags: [sudo]
1363	  community.general.npm:
1364	    name: tldr
1365	    global: true
1366	    state: present
1367	  ignore_errors: true
1368	
1369	# --- tldr (user-level fallback) ---
1370	# Gate broadened to RedHat per pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md — but note this
1371	# uses `mise exec -- npm`, and `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` omits node
1372	# on oldEL (CentOS 7) per the glibc 2.17 baseline. On EL7 mise falls back
1373	# to system node (often missing or too old) and this task no-ops via the
1374	# `mise not found` branch. Live with it; tldr is non-critical.
1375	- name: Re-check if tldr is installed
1376	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
1377	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v tldr
1378	  register: tldr_recheck
1379	  changed_when: false
1380	  failed_when: false
1381	
1382	- name: Install tldr via mise npm (user-level, no sudo)
1383	  when:
1384	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
1385	    - tldr_recheck.rc != 0
1386	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
1387	    if [ -x "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/mise" ]; then
1388	      {{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/mise exec -- npm install -g tldr
1389	    elif command -v mise >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1390	      mise exec -- npm install -g tldr
1391	    else
1392	      echo "mise not found, skipping tldr install" >&2
1393	      exit 0
1394	    fi
1395	  args:
1396	    executable: /bin/bash
1397	  changed_when: true
1398	  ignore_errors: true

1415	    glow_release_arch: >-
1416	      {{
1417	        'x86_64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
1418	        else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
1419	        else 'arm' if target_architecture in ['armv7l', 'armv6l', 'arm']
1420	        else ''
1421	      }}

1430	
1431	- name: Install glow from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
1432	  when:
1433	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
1434	    - glow_check.rc != 0
1435	    - glow_release_arch != ''
1436	  block:
1437	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (glow)
1438	      ansible.builtin.file:
1439	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
1440	        state: directory
1441	        mode: '0755'

1446	        return_content: true
1447	      register: glow_release
1448	
1449	    - name: Set glow version facts
1450	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
1451	        glow_version: "{{ glow_release.json.tag_name | regex_replace('^v', '') }}"
1452	
1453	    - name: Download glow tarball
1454	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
1455	        url: "https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow/releases/download/{{ glow_release.json.tag_name }}/glow_{{ glow_version }}_Linux_{{ glow_release_arch }}.tar.gz"
1456	        dest: /tmp/glow.tar.gz
1457	        mode: '0644'
1458	        timeout: 120
1459	      retries: 3
1460	      delay: 5
1461	
1462	    - name: Create glow temp directory
1463	      ansible.builtin.file:
1464	        path: /tmp/glow
1465	        state: directory
1466	        mode: '0755'
1467	
1468	    - name: Extract glow
1469	      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
1470	        src: /tmp/glow.tar.gz
1471	        dest: /tmp/glow
1472	        remote_src: true
1473	
1474	    - name: Find glow binary

1476	        paths: /tmp/glow
1477	        patterns: glow
1478	        file_type: file
1479	        recurse: true

1491	        mode: '0755'
1492	        remote_src: true

1496	        path: "{{ item }}"
1497	        state: absent

1500	        - /tmp/glow

1504	      ansible.builtin.debug:

1507	    - name: Clean up glow temp files after failure
1508	      ansible.builtin.file:
1509	        path: "{{ item }}"
1510	        state: absent

1513	        - /tmp/glow

.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:181:# Does NOT touch Neovim (~/.config/nvim/) — Neovim is always vim-flavored.
CLAUDE.md:9:When you touch one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror in the same commit.
CLAUDE.md:31:| chezmoi-apply reload hint: `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_99_signal_reload.sh.tmpl` (touches sentinel) ↔ `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh` (reads sentinel + zsh/bash hook registration + `cas`/`cau` wrappers) | Row in [docs/shells/aliases.md](docs/shells/aliases.md) "Dotfiles management" section for `cas`/`cau` | The sentinel path `~/.cache/chezmoi/last-apply` is hard-coded in **two** places — the run-script that touches it and the shared backend that reads it. Keep both in sync when relocating (e.g. switching to `$XDG_STATE_HOME`). Hook registration is in the shared backend (NOT `dot_config/{zsh,bash}/99_*`) because bash's `$BASH_CONFIG_DIR` loads before `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell` (oh-my-bash `plugins=()` prereq, see `dot_bashrc.tmpl:94` vs `:114`), so a per-shell hook file in `dot_config/bash/` would run before the backend function exists. Opt out: `export CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0`. |
CLAUDE.md:49:Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):
CLAUDE.md:129:- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.
CLAUDE.md:183:- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.

<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/image-preview/`

```text
How Yazi picks a display method
- Yazi selects the preview method automatically in a priority order "from top to bottom", using TERM, TERM_PROGRAM and XDG_SESSION_TYPE to detect environment and avoid manual overrides.
- It reports which adapter it chose via the debug output (e.g. Adapter.matches → Kgp, Iip, Sixel, X11, Wayland, Chafa).

Native-protocol vs. window-system vs. fallbacks
- Terminals that natively support image protocols (built-in support listed): kitty, iTerm2, WezTerm, Konsole, foot, Ghostty, Windows Terminal, st (Sixel patch), Warp, Tabby, VSCode, Black Box, Bobcat, etc. (these use Kitty protocol, iTerm2 inline, or Sixel as applicable).
- If running on X11/Wayland Yazi can use the window-system approach; that requires Überzug++ ("Überzug++ required").
- The final fallback is Chafa/ASCII-art when no other method is available; as the docs state: "Chafa is required as the last fallback resort".

When Yazi falls back to Chafa
- Chafa is used only after all higher-priority methods fail or are unavailable (no native protocol, no Überzug++ window option). Quoted: "Chafa is required as the last fallback resort".

Effects of tmux
- tmux can change which protocol actually works: Yazi provides tmux configuration tips to enable passthrough and warns you must restart tmux. Quoted: "To enable Yazi's image preview to work correctly in tmux, add the following 3 options to your `tmux.conf`".
- Some protocols have tmux-specific limitations: the older Kitty protocol variant "KgpOld" does not work under tmux, and Sixel requires tmux to be built with sixel support (pass --enable-sixel) to function inside tmux.

Other notes from the docs
- Yazi will pick the smallest of configured max_width/max_height and the terminal pixel size; some terminals (VSCode, Tabby, Windows terminals) don't expose pixel size via ioctl, so only max_width/max_height are used.
- To see exactly which adapter Yazi picks, run yazi --debug and inspect the Adapter.matches line.

# RedHat (CentOS/Rocky/Alma) base packages. ripgrep + fd skipped here:
# they're EPEL-only on CentOS 7 and the GitHub-release fallback below
# handles them more reliably (musl tarballs ignore glibc 2.17). Skipped
# entirely on noRoot (tags: [sudo] → --skip-tags sudo).
#
# Why `command: yum install` instead of `ansible.builtin.yum:`?
# ansible-core 2.18+ collapsed the yum module into a wrapper that
# routes through the dnf module backend. On CentOS 7 there is no `dnf`
# binary, so `ansible.builtin.yum:` aborts with
# `Could not detect which major revision of dnf is in use`. Rocky/Alma 8+
# do ship dnf, but using yum CLI works on both — see
# pitfalls/centos7-ansible-yum-dnf-backend.md.
- name: Install base packages (RedHat/CentOS) — yum CLI for CentOS 7 + Rocky/Alma compat
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  # Why `${missing[*]:-}` instead of `${#missing[@]}`?
  # Jinja2 templating in ansible reads `${#...}` as a comment block
  # (`{# ... #}` in Jinja syntax) and aborts with "unbalanced jinja2 block".
  # `${missing[*]:-}` expands to space-joined elements (empty when unset)
  # so `[ -z ... ]` cleanly tests "any missing packages" without `{#`.
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -e
    missing=()
    for p in git git-lfs curl wget jq tree gcc gcc-c++ make; do
      rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
    done
    if [ -z "${missing[*]:-}" ]; then
      echo "ALL_INSTALLED"
      exit 0
    fi
    yum install -y "${missing[@]}"
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  register: base_yum_result
  changed_when: "'ALL_INSTALLED' not in base_yum_result.stdout"
  ignore_errors: true

# --- ripgrep (user-level fallback) ---

**Linux block (lines 144–end) — per-tool, not a list.** Header at line 144 (`# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)`). Each tool is its own sequence with several mechanisms mixed:
- **apt** (`ansible.builtin.apt`, `become: true`, `tags: [sudo]`) — e.g. bat (444–450), bats (548–554).
- **Linuxbrew fallback** — probe `command -v brew || true`, then `community.general.homebrew` if present. E.g. bat (462–476), eza aarch64 (802–822), git-delta aarch64 (911–931).
- **GitHub/GitLab release** — `uri` to the `.../releases/latest` API → `get_url` a `.deb` (installed via apt) or a tarball/zip extracted to `~/.local/bin`. E.g. gh (180–294), glab (327–441), diffnav, git-graph, glow, gum, vhs, freeze, **yazi**.

- **npm / mise** — tldr (1356–1398).
- **Two-tier pattern**: a sudo `.deb`/apt path first (Debian only, `tags:[sudo]`), then a user-level `~/.local/bin` fallback (usually broadened to `["Debian","RedHat"]`, musl binaries), each wrapped in `block:`/`rescue:` that just warns + cleans up `/tmp` on failure.
