--- dot_ansible/roles/media_tools/tasks/main.yml ---
---
# Media / AV CLI tools role
# Tools: ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips
# ffmpeg is also vhs's runtime dependency — see dot_ansible/roles/devtools/
# tasks/main.yml `# --- vhs ---` block.
#
# noRoot=true on Linux: the upstream run_onchange script injects
# `--skip-tags sudo`, which strips the apt block below (it carries
# `tags: [sudo]`). No extra in-role guard needed; user-level fallbacks
# would be impractical for these packages (ffmpeg / imagemagick / libvips
# all want C compilers + system codecs).

# =============================================================================
# macOS — all via Homebrew
# =============================================================================

- name: Install media/AV tools (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - ffmpeg        # provides ffmpeg, ffprobe, ffplay
      - imagemagick   # v7 unified `magick` binary (also ships `convert` shim)
      - exiftool
      - vips          # provides vips, vipsthumbnail, vipsedit
    state: present

# =============================================================================
# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) — apt
# =============================================================================

- name: Install media/AV tools from apt (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - ffmpeg                       # ffmpeg + ffprobe + ffplay
      - imagemagick                  # Ubuntu 24.04 ships v6 → /usr/bin/convert
      - libimage-exiftool-perl       # provides /usr/bin/exiftool
      - libvips-tools                # vips, vipsthumbnail, vipsedit
    state: present
    # Don't re-run apt-get update here: these are all main-archive/universe
    # packages already covered by the base role's best-effort cache refresh at
    # play start. An inlined update_cache would let a single transient
    # proxy/source failure abort the whole play (it did on a flaky proxy).
    # See pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md.
    update_cache: false

# Maximize Yazi Preview Coverage (images / PDF / video / archives / SVG / EPUB / dmg)

## Context

Yazi today only previews tabular/office files (duckdb.yazi + `view-office`). Everything else
falls through to yazi's **built-in** previewers, which shell out to external binaries at
runtime — and most of those binaries aren't installed by this repo, so on hover the user sees:

- **`failed to spawn chafa`** on png/pdf/mp4/HEIC — yazi's built-ins rasterize each to an image,
  then display it via the adapter it auto-selects. With no native graphics protocol available
  (e.g. inside tmux, or a non-graphics terminal) that adapter is **chafa** (yazi's documented
  "last fallback resort"), which isn't installed. One missing tool breaks *all* image-derived
  previews at the shared display step.
- **`failed to start either 7zz or 7z. Do you have 7-zip installed?`** — no 7-Zip → no archive
  or dmg preview.
- **EPUB / dmg → bare file-type classification** — their mimes (`application/epub+zip`,
  `application/x-apple-diskimage`) aren't in yazi's built-in archive set.

**Root cause is tool-install, not config** — nothing in `dot_config/yazi/` names these tools
(confirmed by full grep). Fix = install yazi's documented optional deps across macOS + Linux,
plus two tiny `piper` rules for the two container formats yazi ignores by default.

Coverage matrix (verified against yazi upstream docs + this host, Intel mac, yazi 26.1.22):

| Preview | Needs | Repo status |
|---|---|---|
| png/jpg/webp/gif  **+ the display step of every image-derived preview** | **chafa** | missing → baseline adds |
| PDF | poppler (`pdftoppm`) + chafa | poppler unmanaged → baseline adds |
| archives (zip/tar/7z/rar/gz…) **+ dmg** | **7-Zip** | missing → baseline adds |
| SVG | resvg + chafa | missing → baseline adds |
| video (`.mp4`) | ffmpeg + chafa | ffmpeg **gated** behind `installMediaTools` |
| HEIC / JPEG-XL / fonts | ImageMagick ≥7.1.1 + chafa | **gated** behind `installMediaTools` |
| json / text / std images | jq / built-in | already always-installed |

**User decisions:** (1) keep ffmpeg + ImageMagick **gated** behind `installMediaTools`
(default off; forced off on server/minimal) — just document the yazi tie-in. (2) **Add EPUB + dmg
previewer rules** (pandoc is already installed everywhere; 7zip lands in the baseline → no new
install cost).

## Changes

### 1. Baseline preview deps — `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (always-installed, next to yazi)

- **macOS** — add to the single big brew `name:` list (~L57-125): `chafa`, `poppler`,
  `sevenzip` (provides `7zz`), `resvg`. Update the `# Tools:` header comment (L3).
- **Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)** — new `# --- yazi preview deps ---` block near the yazi section (~L2227):
  - apt (`become: true`, `tags: [sudo]`): `chafa`, `poppler-utils`, `p7zip-full` (provides `7z`;
    yazi accepts `7zz` **or** `7z`).
  - `resvg` has no apt package → best-effort **linuxbrew** (`community.general.homebrew`) else
    `cargo install resvg`, wrapped `block:`/`rescue:`→warn (matches the eza/git-delta aarch64
    fallback idiom already in this file). SVG preview is simply absent if it can't install — non-fatal.

  These are **not** gated on `primary_shell`/`installMediaTools` — small, universally useful, and
  the direct fix for the reported errors on every machine.

### 2. EPUB + dmg previewer rules — `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml`

Append to the existing `prepend_previewers` list. `piper` is already pinned → **no** new plugin,
**no** `init.lua`/`package.toml`/run-script change:

\```toml
{ url = "*.epub", run = 'piper -- pandoc -f epub -t plain "$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
{ url = "*.dmg",  run = 'piper -- ( 7zz l "$1" 2>/dev/null || 7z l "$1" 2>/dev/null ) | head -n 200' },
\```

- `2>/dev/null` is **load-bearing** — piper renders any stderr as an error preview (same rule as
  the existing feather/sqlite fallbacks).
- `7zz || 7z` covers macOS `sevenzip` (`7zz`) vs Linux `p7zip-full` (`7z`).
- `.apk/.jar/.whl/.xpi/.zip/.tar.*` need **no** rule — yazi's built-in archive previewer handles
  them free once 7-Zip is installed (document this, don't add rules).

### 3. Docs (CLAUDE.md cross-file rules mandate same-commit updates)

- **NEW `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`** — umbrella "yazi preview coverage" page: the
  format→tool→tier matrix above; the chafa-fallback explanation + native-protocol/tmux note
  (install a graphics terminal to auto-upgrade from ascii-art); the `installMediaTools` gating for
  video/HEIC **and** the Ubuntu-ImageMagick-v6 HEIC caveat; the EPUB/dmg rules; per-OS install
  (brew formulae vs apt packages vs resvg fallback). Cross-link ↔ `office-viewers.md`,
  `data-viewers.md`. Pitfall/repo-root links use absolute GitHub URLs (repo convention).
- **`mkdocs.yml`** — nav entry (en + zh-TW) next to Office/Data viewers; then
  `uv run mkdocs build --strict`.
- **`docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`** — A–Z index rows: `chafa`, `poppler`, `sevenzip`/`7zip`,
  `resvg` (mechanism: **devtools** — brew macOS / apt Linux); update the devtools Tools list.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — extend the existing yazi-preview contract row: add the `yazi-previews.md`
  reference, the runtime-tool deps (chafa/poppler/7zip/resvg always; ffmpeg/ImageMagick gated), and
  the two new epub/dmg piper rules.
- **`README.md`** — extend the yazi/preview bullet: images, PDF, video, archives, ebooks.

## Critical files

- **Functional:** `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`, `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml`
- **Reused as-is (no edit):** `dot_config/yazi/{init.lua,package.toml,keymap.toml}`, `piper` plugin,
  `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl`, the `media_tools` role
  (ffmpeg/ImageMagick stay gated — deliberate)
- **Docs:** new `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`, `mkdocs.yml`, `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`,
  `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`

## Verification

1. **Confirm formula names + the fix on this mac:** `brew install chafa poppler sevenzip resvg`
   then `command -v chafa 7zz pdftoppm resvg`. (This mac already has ffmpeg/magick, so pdf/mp4/heic
   should render as soon as chafa is present.)
2. **Parse gate:** `taplo check dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` + `python3 -c 'import tomllib …'`.
3. **Ansible:** `ansible-playbook --syntax-check` the devtools role; run the new tasks narrowly
   (`--tags`/check-mode) where possible. If a host/cred is missing, say so explicitly.
4. **Docs:** `uv run mkdocs build --strict`.
5. **Piper-command sanity (headless-OK):** run each new rule body standalone —
   `pandoc -f epub -t plain book.epub | head`, `7zz l some.dmg | head`.
6. **Real-terminal smoke (can't run headless — sandbox yazi aborts with os error 6):** launch
   `yazi` and hover a png / pdf / mp4 / .zip / .dmg / .epub / .svg / .heic. Expect
   images/pdf/video as chafa ascii-art (or inline in a graphics terminal), archive + dmg listings,
   epub text, svg render. Confirm a plain `.txt`/`.json` still previews normally.

## Notes / follow-ups

- **Native inline images vs chafa:** chafa gives universal ascii-art previews (works over
  tmux/ssh/any terminal). For crisp inline images use a graphics-capable terminal
  (Ghostty/Kitty/iTerm2/WezTerm) — yazi auto-upgrades the adapter; over tmux the terminal must
  support Kitty-graphics passthrough (repo already sets `allow-passthrough on`). Documented, not coded.
- **Ubuntu HEIC/font:** apt ImageMagick is v6 (no unified `magick`, weak HEIC) → those previews may
  not work on Ubuntu even with `installMediaTools=true`. Documented as a known caveat; v7 needs a
  PPA/build (out of scope).

 `./docs/tools/data-viewers.md`

```text
1	# View Data Files in the Terminal
2	
3	Preview and explore tabular / data files — **CSV**, **TSV**, **Parquet**, **Feather/Arrow**,
4	**Excel `.xlsx`**, **SQLite**, and native **DuckDB** databases — without leaving the terminal, and
5	without opening an editor or a GUI.
6	
7	Two layers:
8	
9	- **Inline previews** in the [yazi](tmux/README.md) file manager — hover a data file and its rows
10	  render as an aligned table in the right pane, powered by the [`duckdb.yazi`](#duckdbyazi--the-previewer)
11	  plugin (with two small fallbacks for the formats DuckDB can't read).
12	- **Interactive exploration** with [VisiData](#visidata--interactive-exploration) (`vd`) — a fast,
13	  vim-keyed spreadsheet TUI for sorting, filtering, frequency tables, and describe.
14	
15	The split is deliberate: **DuckDB for the glance, VisiData for the deep-dive.** We evaluated using
16	VisiData for previews too and rejected it — its non-interactive batch output is raw TSV (or a
17	`--save-filetype fixed` monochrome table), it can't preview SQLite data (only lists tables), can't
18	open `.xlsx` (its tool venv has no `openpyxl`), and is slow on the preview hot-path (~0.4 s for CSV,
19	up to ~10 s cold for parquet, because it imports pandas + pyarrow). DuckDB's `-box` renders a native
20	aligned table in ~0.1 s and can cheaply `LIMIT` to the first N rows.
21	
22	## TL;DR
23	
24	| Format | yazi preview | Engine |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| `.csv` `.tsv` | ✅ table | duckdb.yazi |
27	| `.parquet` | ✅ table | duckdb.yazi |
28	| `.xlsx` | ✅ table | duckdb.yazi (DuckDB `spatial` ext — see gotcha) |
29	| `.db` `.duckdb` | ✅ table listing | duckdb.yazi (DuckDB auto-attaches SQLite) |
30	| `.sqlite` `.sqlite3` | ✅ table listing | piper → `duckdb -readonly` (fallback) |
31	| `.feather` `.arrow` | ✅ table | piper → VisiData `fixed` (DuckDB has no Arrow-IPC reader) |
32	
33	All formats open interactively in **VisiData** (`vd <file>`) regardless of the preview engine.
34	
35	## `duckdb.yazi` — the previewer
36	
37	[`duckdb.yazi`](https://github.com/wylie102/duckdb.yazi) is a Yazi previewer/preloader plugin that
38	shells out to the **`duckdb` CLI** (already installed by the `devtools` role) and renders its `-box`
39	table into the preview pane. It reads CSV, TSV, Parquet, Excel, and DuckDB/SQLite databases.
40	
41	Three pieces make it work in this repo:
42	
43	| Piece | Path | Role |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| Lockfile (SSOT) | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml` | pins `wylie102/duckdb` (rev + hash) |
46	| Init | `dot_config/yazi/init.lua` | **required** `require("duckdb"):setup({ mode = "standard" })` |
47	| Wiring | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin]` | `prepend_previewers` + `prepend_preloaders` (`run = "duckdb"`) |
48	
49	The `setup()` call in `init.lua` is mandatory — without it the `run = "duckdb"` rules never activate.
50	We set `mode = "standard"` so hover shows actual data rows (the plugin default is `summarized`); press
51	`K` at the top of a preview to toggle to DuckDB's `SUMMARIZE` view (min/max/counts per column).
52	
53	### Keybindings
54	
55	Added to `dot_config/yazi/keymap.toml` (`[mgr] prepend_keymap`):
56	
57	| Key | Action |
58	|---|---|
59	| `K` | Toggle standard ⇄ SUMMARIZE view (built into the plugin; no keymap entry) |
60	| `H` / `L` | Scroll one column left / right in the preview |
61	| `g o` | Open the hovered file in the DuckDB CLI |
62	| `g u` | Open the hovered file in the DuckDB UI |
63	
64	> ⚠ **`H` / `L` override Yazi's default history back/forward** (the capital-letter binds). Lowercase
65	> `h` / `l` (leave / enter directory) are unaffected. On non-data files `H`/`L` no-op.
66	
67	### The two fallbacks (formats DuckDB can't read)
68	
69	- **Feather / Arrow** (`.feather` `.arrow`) — DuckDB has no Arrow-IPC file reader, so these route
70	  through [`piper.yazi`](office-viewers.md#the-ya-pkg-plugin-mechanism) to VisiData's non-interactive
71	  `fixed` saver:
72	  ```toml
73	  { url = "*.feather", run = 'piper -- vd -b -f arrow "$1" -o - --save-filetype fixed 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' }
74	  ```
75	  `-f arrow` forces the pure-pyarrow `ArrowSheet` loader (dodges the pandas `StringDtype` crash — see
76	  [the feather pitfall](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md)), and `2>/dev/null`
77	  is **mandatory**: piper renders any stderr as an error preview, and VisiData logs status to stderr.
78	- **SQLite by `.sqlite` / `.sqlite3` name** — the plugin's internal `extension_map` only knows `.db`
79	  (not `.sqlite`), so those two extensions route through piper to a `duckdb -readonly` table listing.
80	  Plain `.db` gets the full plugin treatment (DuckDB transparently attaches SQLite databases opened
81	  directly, so `.db` covers most SQLite files).
82	
83	## VisiData — interactive exploration
84	
85	`vd <file>` opens a full-screen, vim-keyed spreadsheet over CSV/TSV/JSON/Parquet/Feather/Arrow/xlsx/
86	SQLite. This is the tool for actual analysis: sort, filter (`|` / `\`), frequency (`Shift+F`),
87	describe (`Shift+I`), pivot, and save-as. Defaults are already vim-flavored (`h/j/k/l`, `gg/G`,
88	`/?` search); the repo adds strict-vim column nav under `enableVimMode`. See
89	[aliases.md → Data Viewers](../shells/aliases.md#data-viewers) for the `vd-arrow` / `vd-ro` wrappers
90	and [vim-mode.md → VisiData](../this_repo/vim-mode.md#visidata) for the key rebinds.
91	
92	VisiData and its companion `~/.visidatarc` are installed/managed regardless (`visidata` is a required
93	uv tool with `pandas` + `pyarrow`); the `.visidatarc` carries the `.feather` → `ArrowSheet` reroute
94	that the preview fallback above also relies on.
95	
96	## Where things live
97	
98	| Surface | Path |
99	|---|---|
100	| Plugin lockfile + installer | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` |
101	| Plugin init | `dot_config/yazi/init.lua` |
102	| Previewers + preloaders | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin]` |
103	| Keybindings | `dot_config/yazi/keymap.toml` |
104	| DuckDB CLI install | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
105	| VisiData install + rc | `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`, `dot_visidatarc.tmpl` |
106	| Upgrades | `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`) |
107	
108	## Gotchas
109	
110	- **`.xlsx` first preview needs internet.** duckdb.yazi reads Excel via DuckDB's `spatial` extension,
111	  which it `INSTALL`s on first use — the first `.xlsx` preview on a fresh machine downloads it (cached
112	  in `~/.duckdb` afterwards). CSV/TSV/Parquet/DB previews use built-ins and need no network.
113	- **`.xlsx` preview moved off `view-office`.** Yazi now previews `.xlsx` with duckdb.yazi, not
114	  `markitdown`. The `view-office --preview budget.xlsx` **CLI** is unchanged (still markitdown → glow);
115	  only Yazi's previewer wiring moved. See [office-viewers.md](office-viewers.md).
116	- **Lowercase globs.** The `url` globs are lowercase (`*.csv`); a file named `DATA.CSV` won't trigger
117	  the previewer. (VisiData opened directly still works.)
118	- **DuckDB normalizes display.** `-box` may render `1200.50` as `1200.5` (type inference) — it's a
119	  display artifact of the preview, not a change to the file.
120	- **`view-office` for `.xls`/`.ods`.** Legacy binary `.xls` and OpenDocument `.ods` stay on the
121	  LibreOffice → OOXML path (DuckDB can't read those); only modern `.xlsx` uses duckdb.yazi.
122	
123	## See also
124	
125	- [Office viewers](office-viewers.md) — the `.docx/.pptx` + legacy/ODF sibling stack (doxx / markitdown / LibreOffice), and the `ya pkg` / `piper.yazi` mechanism shared here.
126	- [Data Viewers (aliases)](../shells/aliases.md#data-viewers) — VisiData `vd-arrow` / `vd-ro` wrappers.
127	- [tool-managers.md § 15](../this_repo/tool-managers.md) — `ya pkg` plugin mechanism (piper.yazi, duckdb.yazi).
128	- [Feather / StringDtype pitfall](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md) — why `.feather` needs the ArrowSheet loader.
129
```
</details></tool-use>

```md
# Yazi Preview Coverage

Maximize what the [yazi](tmux/README.md) file manager can preview on hover — **images, PDF, video,
SVG, archives, ebooks, dmg**, on top of the tabular/office stacks documented in
[data-viewers.md](data-viewers.md) and [office-viewers.md](office-viewers.md).

The catch: yazi's **built-in** previewers (images / PDF / video / SVG / standard archives) are *not*
wired in `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` — yazi ships them internally and **shells out to external
binaries at runtime**. If those binaries aren't installed, the hover pane shows an error
(`failed to spawn chafa`) or bare file-type classification. So "expanding coverage" is mostly a
**tool-install** job (a few ansible-managed binaries), plus two tiny config rules for the container
formats yazi ignores by default.

## TL;DR — coverage matrix

| File type | Preview | Powered by | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| png / jpg / webp / gif / bmp | image (or unicode-art) | yazi built-in → **chafa** to display | baseline |
| **PDF** | first page as image | yazi built-in → **poppler** (`pdftoppm`) + chafa | baseline |
| **SVG** | rendered image | yazi built-in → **resvg** + chafa | baseline |
| archives: zip / tar / gz / 7z / rar (+ zip-based apk / jar / whl / xpi) | file listing | yazi built-in → **7-Zip** | baseline |
| **dmg** | file listing | piper → **7-Zip** (`*.dmg` rule) | baseline |
| **EPUB** | text | piper → **pandoc** (`*.epub` rule) | baseline |
| video: mp4 / mkv / mov … | thumbnail | yazi built-in → **ffmpeg** + chafa | media (gated) |
| HEIC / JPEG-XL / fonts | image / sample | yazi built-in → **ImageMagick ≥7.1.1** + chafa | media (gated) |
| csv / tsv / parquet / xlsx / db / sqlite / feather | table | duckdb.yazi + fallbacks | plugin — see [data-viewers.md](data-viewers.md) |
| docx / pptx / legacy / ODF | rendered text | view-office (doxx / markitdown / LibreOffice) | plugin — see [office-viewers.md](office-viewers.md) |
| txt / json / md / source | text (+ syntax) | yazi built-in / `bat` | always |

- **Baseline** tools are installed unconditionally by the `devtools` role (next to yazi).
- **Media (gated)** tools live in the `media_tools` role behind the `installMediaTools` prompt
  (default **off**; forced off on server/minimal). Video + HEIC previews work only where you opted in.

## Why images showed `failed to spawn chafa`

Every image-derived preview funnels through the same final **display** step. yazi renders png (direct),
PDF (via poppler), video (via ffmpeg), HEIC (via ImageMagick), SVG (via resvg) all *to an image*, then
hands that image to the display adapter it auto-selected. yazi picks the adapter from your terminal:
Kitty graphics protocol, iTerm2 inline, Sixel, Überzug++ (X11/Wayland), and — when none of those is
available (a non-graphics terminal, or inside tmux without passthrough) — **chafa**, its documented
*"last fallback resort"* that draws the image as Unicode/ANSI art.

So a missing `chafa` breaks **all** of png/pdf/mp4/HEIC at once, even though poppler/ffmpeg/magick are
present — they produce the image fine; nothing can display it. Installing `chafa` fixes the whole set.

### Unicode-art vs crisp inline images

chafa gives **universal ASCII/ANSI-art** previews that work everywhere — over tmux, over SSH, in any
terminal. For crisp *inline* images, run yazi in a graphics-capable terminal
(**Ghostty / Kitty / iTerm2 / WezTerm / Konsole / foot / Ghostty**); yazi auto-upgrades the adapter,
no config change. Over tmux the terminal must support Kitty-graphics passthrough — this repo already
sets `allow-passthrough on` (`dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl`), but the older `KgpOld` protocol
variant doesn't work under tmux and Sixel needs a `--enable-sixel` tmux build. If you only ever get
ascii-art, that's the terminal/tmux graphics story, **not** a missing tool — chafa is doing its job.
See yazi's [image-preview docs](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/image-preview/).

## The two config rules (EPUB + dmg)

Everything above except EPUB and dmg is pure tool-install — yazi's built-ins handle the routing. Those
two container mimes (`application/epub+zip`, `application/x-apple-diskimage`) are **not** in yazi's
built-in archive set, so `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` adds them via [`piper.yazi`](office-viewers.md#the-ya-pkg-plugin-mechanism):

\```toml
{ url = "*.epub", run = 'piper -- pandoc -f epub -t plain "$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
{ url = "*.dmg",  run = 'piper -- ( 7zz l "$1" 2>/dev/null || 7z l "$1" 2>/dev/null ) | head -n 200' },
\```

- `2>/dev/null` is **load-bearing** — piper renders any stderr as an error preview.
- `7zz || 7z` covers macOS `sevenzip` (`7zz`) vs Linux `p7zip-full` (`7z`).
- **No rule needed** for `.zip` / `.tar.*` / `.7z` / `.rar` or zip-based `.apk` / `.jar` / `.whl` /
  `.xpi` — yazi's built-in archive previewer lists them for free once 7-Zip is installed.

## Per-OS install

| Tool | macOS (brew, `devtools`) | Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) | Enables |
|---|---|---|---|
| **chafa** | `chafa` | apt `chafa` | image display fallback (all image-derived previews) |
| **poppler** | `poppler` | apt `poppler-utils` | PDF |
| **7-Zip** | `sevenzip` (`7zz`) | apt `p7zip-full` (`7z`) | archives + dmg |
| **resvg** | `resvg` | Linuxbrew → `cargo install resvg` (no apt pkg; non-fatal if absent) | SVG |
| ffmpeg | `ffmpeg` (`media_tools`, gated) | apt `ffmpeg` (gated) | video thumbnails |
| ImageMagick | `imagemagick` (`media_tools`, gated) | apt `imagemagick` (gated) | HEIC / JPEG-XL / fonts |
| pandoc | `pandoc` (already in `devtools`) | apt `pandoc` | EPUB text |

## Gotchas

- **Ubuntu ImageMagick is v6.** apt ships ImageMagick 6 (no unified `magick`; weak HEIC), so HEIC/font
  previews may not work on Ubuntu even with `installMediaTools=true`. yazi wants **≥7.1.1**; v7 needs a
  PPA or source build (out of scope). macOS brew ImageMagick is v7 → fine.
- **Video/HEIC need `installMediaTools`.** ffmpeg + ImageMagick are opt-in. If mp4 thumbnails or HEIC
  previews are blank, re-run init with `installMediaTools=true` (or install ffmpeg/imagemagick by
  hand). Everything else in the baseline works without it.
- **resvg on Linux is best-effort.** No apt package → the role tries Linuxbrew then a one-time
  `cargo install resvg`. If neither is available, SVG simply previews as raw text — non-fatal.
- **Lowercase globs.** The `*.epub` / `*.dmg` rules match lowercase extensions; `Book.EPUB` won't fire
  (yazi's built-ins are mime-based and unaffected).
- **chafa is a fallback, not a downgrade to avoid.** ascii-art is the correct behavior in a
  non-graphics terminal — see [above](#unicode-art-vs-crisp-inline-images).

## Where things live

| Surface | Path |
|---|---|
| Baseline tool install (chafa/poppler/7zip/resvg) | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
| Media tool install (ffmpeg/ImageMagick, gated) | `dot_ansible/roles/media_tools/tasks/main.yml` |
| EPUB + dmg previewer rules | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin] prepend_previewers` |
| yazi install | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (`# --- yazi ---`) |
| tmux image passthrough | `dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl` (`allow-passthrough on`) |

## See also

- [Data viewers](data-viewers.md) — the csv/parquet/xlsx/sqlite/feather table-preview stack (duckdb.yazi).
- [Office viewers](office-viewers.md) — the docx/pptx/legacy/ODF stack + the shared `ya pkg` / `piper.yazi` mechanism.
- [tool-managers.md § Tool index](../this_repo/tool-managers.md#tool-index-az) — where chafa / poppler / sevenzip / resvg come from per OS.
- yazi upstream: [installation deps](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/installation/), [image preview](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/image-preview/).

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I'm adding a new row to the CLAUDE.md documentation for yazi's built-in preview capabilities, positioning it after the data-file viewing section. This entry will reference the configuration files that enable image, PDF, video, archive, SVG, EPUB, and DMG previews through tools like chafa, poppler, sevenzip, and resvg.

The key contract here is that yazi shells out to these external tools at runtime rather than having them wired directly into the config. Chafa serves as the universal image fallback, so its absence breaks all image/PDF/video/HEIC previews. The baseline tools (chafa, poppler, 7zip, resvg) are always installed via devtools, while ffmpeg and imagemagick are gated behind the installMediaTools flag to avoid duplication. For EPUB files, pandoc handles conversion; for DMG files, either 7zz (macOS) or 7z (Linux) is used with stderr suppressed. I'm anchoring this new row to the end of line 25 and constructing it as a single table line. Yazi's built-in previewers are a tool-install contract rather than a configuration one—yazi ships them and invokes them at runtime, so they need to be present on the system. Chafa serves as the fallback for image display when native graphics protocols aren't available (like in tmux), and if it's missing, all image, PDF, video, and HEIC previews fail.

The baseline toolset that should always be installed includes chafa, poppler, sevenzip, and resvg, while ffmpeg and ImageMagick for video and HEIC handling stay optional behind a flag. For EPUB files, I'm using pandoc to convert to plain text; for DMG files, I'm trying sevenzip with a fallback and suppressing stderr since piper treats it as an error. Built-in archive formats like zip, tar, apk, jar, and whl don't need explicit rules.
</details></think>

Summary of the top findings
- Chafa added terminal probing controls: a generic --probe option (auto/on/off) and a --probe-mode option (any|ctty|stdio). You can disable probing entirely with --probe=off, or change how chafa probes the terminal with --probe-mode (e.g. probe the controlling tty or only stdio). ([hpjansson.org](https://hpjansson.org/chafa/man/))
- OSC 10/11 are the standard OSC sequences used to query the terminal’s foreground/background colors — these are commonly used by apps to detect light/dark themes. ([vtdn.dev](https://vtdn.dev/docs/osc/osc11/))
- Several projects/terminals have reported a class of bugs where OSC 10/11 (and other query) responses are delivered into a child process’s stdin (visible as text in panes/shells) instead of being consumed by the querying program. Examples: issues reported in zellij, agenthub and other terminal front-ends. This is a terminal/multiplexer-side leak/regression, not unique to chafa. ([github.com](https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/issues/5138))

Practical fixes / mitigations
- To avoid any terminal probing (and therefore avoid OSC 10/11 queries/responses), run chafa with probing disabled:
  - chafa --probe=off <image>
  This disables color probing entirely. ([hpjansson.org](https://hpjansson.org/chafa/man/))
- If you still want probing but want to avoid interfering with stdin/stdout pipelines, try changing probe mode:
  - chafa --probe-mode=ctty <image>  (probe /dev/tty / controlling tty)
  - chafa --probe-mode=stdio <image> (only use stdio)
  Choose the mode that best matches how you run chafa (e.g., in pipelines or inside multiplexers). ([hpjansson.org](https://hpjansson.org/chafa/man/))
- If the leak is occurring inside a terminal multiplexer or web/agent surface, the longer-term fix is to update the terminal/multiplexer (zellij, the web relay, etc.) once upstream patches are released; the issue is widely reported in those projects' issue trackers. <tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# chafa wrapper — force `--probe off`.
#
# WHY: yazi's fallback image adapter shells out to `chafa` for terminals with no
# native graphics protocol (e.g. Alacritty) and there is no way to pass it flags.
# chafa >=1.16 probes the terminal for its fg/bg colors via OSC 10/11 queries;
# inside tmux/zellij chafa often exits before the multiplexer delivers the reply,
# so the terminal's `rgb:…` response leaks into yazi's input buffer and pops a
# spurious rename / shell prompt (yazi #3680 — closed "not planned": it's a mux
# leak; chafa's `--probe off` is the source-side cure). `--probe off` only skips
# color auto-detection (chafa falls back to sensible defaults from $TERM/
# $COLORTERM), so ascii-art previews are unchanged.
#
# INERT on graphics terminals (Ghostty/Kitty/iTerm2/…): yazi uses the native
# protocol there and never calls chafa, so this shim is a no-op cost. It lives on
# ~/.dotfiles/bin, which precedes brew on PATH (dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl).
# See docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
set -e

# Resolve the REAL chafa (this shim's dir is never in the list → no recursion).
real=""
for c in /opt/homebrew/bin/chafa /usr/local/bin/chafa \
         /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/chafa "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/chafa" \
         /usr/bin/chafa; do
  [ -x "$c" ] && { real="$c"; break; }
done
if [ -z "$real" ]; then
  # Fallback: first `chafa` on PATH outside this wrapper's own directory.
  selfdir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
  IFS=:
  for d in $PATH; do
    [ "$d" = "$selfdir" ] && continue
    [ -x "$d/chafa" ] && { real="$d/chafa"; break; }
  done
  unset IFS
fi
[ -n "$real" ] || { echo "chafa (yazi shim): real chafa not found on PATH" >&2; exit 127; }

# Drop any caller-supplied --probe (space- or =-form), then force it off.
args=()
skip=0
for a in "$@"; do
  [ "$skip" = 1 ] && { skip=0; continue; }
  case "$a" in
    --probe)   skip=1 ;;
    --probe=*) ;;
    *) args+=("$a") ;;
  esac
done
exec "$real" "${args[@]}" --probe off

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-16 12:31:14Z)**_

Fixed and verified. Docs still build with only the 12 baseline warnings (none reference the new content).

## What that popup actually was

You didn't trigger a rename or shell — that `rgb:d8d8/d8d8/d8d8…11;rgb:1818/1818/1818` is your **terminal's reply to chafa's OSC 10/11 color queries** (foreground `#d8d8d8`, background `#181818`), with the escape framing stripped, leaking into yazi as if you'd typed it. Different leaked bytes hit different yazi keys — hence sometimes a rename box, sometimes the `Shell:` prompt. Same root cause.

## Why it happened

- **Alacritty has no image graphics protocol**, so yazi must use its **chafa** fallback for image/PDF/video/HEIC/SVG.
- chafa ≥1.16 **probes** the terminal for its colors on every render. Inside **tmux**, chafa often exits before tmux delivers the reply, so tmux hands the `rgb:…` bytes to whatever now owns the tty — yazi — which reads them as keystrokes. Upstream ([yazi #3680](https://github.com/sxyazi/yazi/issues/3680)) closed this "not planned," calling it a multiplexer leak.

## The fix (live now)

A `chafa` wrapper at **`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_chafa`** → `~/.dotfiles/bin/chafa` (ahead of brew on your PATH) that forces **`--probe off`**. chafa never sends the query, so nothing leaks. It's transparent (delegates to brew's chafa), inert on graphics-capable terminals, and previews are otherwise unchanged. Verified: the shim strips any caller `--probe`, appends `--probe off`, and still renders.

**Try it:** just re-hover a `.png`/`.pdf` (restart yazi if your session cached the old lookup). The popup should be gone.

## Files touched for this fix
- `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_chafa` (new shim) — deployed
- `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md` (new "chafa probe leak" section + gotcha)
- `CLAUDE.md` + `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` (recorded the shim so it isn't "cleaned up" later)

Still **uncommitted** — this fix plus the earlier preview-coverage work are all staged-in-tree but not committed. Want me to commit everything together (the coverage feature + this bug fix), or keep them as separate commits?

Sources: [yazi #3680](https://github.com/sxyazi/yazi/issues/3680), [zellij #5138](https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/issues/5138), [chafa man page (`--probe`)](https://hpjansson.org/chafa/man/), [yazi image-preview docs](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/image-preview/).

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# view-office — open or preview Microsoft Office / OpenDocument files in the
3	# terminal. Dispatches by extension to the right tool:
4	#   .docx → doxx        .xlsx → visidata (vd)   .pptx → markitdown | glow
5	#   legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt/.odt/.ods/.odp/.rtf → LibreOffice headless converts to
6	#   the modern OOXML twin, then re-dispatches to the handler above.
7	#
8	# Two modes:
9	#   view-office FILE              interactive TUI / pager (default)
10	#   view-office --preview FILE    non-interactive ANSI/markdown to stdout
11	#
12	# Deliberately plain bash, NOT the `uv run --script` self-boot pattern used by
13	# executable_pqsum / yth / mlf: this sits on yazi's preview hot-path (invoked on
14	# every file hover via the piper.yazi previewer), where uv/Python startup
15	# (~100-200ms) would make previews feel laggy. Pure dispatch/exec is ~5ms.
16	#
17	# The yazi previewer contract (dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml) is:
18	#   run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"'
19	# Keep --preview/--width in sync with that. See docs/tools/office-viewers.md.
20	set -euo pipefail
21	
22	PREVIEW=0
23	WIDTH="${COLUMNS:-100}"
24	
25	usage() {
26	    printf '%s\n' \
27	        "Usage: view-office [--preview] [--width N] FILE" \
28	        "" \
29	        "Open or preview an Office / OpenDocument file in the terminal." \
30	        "" \
31	        "Options:" \
32	        "  -p, --preview    Render to stdout (ANSI/markdown) instead of a TUI." \
33	        "  -w, --width N    Wrap width for --preview (default: \$COLUMNS or 100)." \
34	        "  -h, --help       Show this help." \
35	        "" \
36	        "Formats:" \
37	        "  .docx  doxx (interactive) / doxx --export ansi (preview)" \
38	        "  .xlsx  visidata vd (interactive) / markitdown | glow (preview)" \
39	        "  .pptx  markitdown | glow pager (interactive) / markitdown | glow (preview)" \
40	        "  .doc .xls .ppt .odt .ods .odp .rtf  LibreOffice → OOXML twin, then above"
41	}
42	
43	err() { printf 'view-office: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
44	
45	have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
46	
47	# need TOOL "install hint" — fail with an actionable message if TOOL is absent.
48	need() {
49	    have "$1" && return 0
50	    err "$1 not found — $2"
51	    exit 2
52	}
53	
54	# Resolve the LibreOffice headless binary: `soffice` / `libreoffice` on PATH,
55	# else the macOS .app bundle (the cask does not put soffice on PATH).
56	soffice_bin() {
57	    local b
58	    for b in soffice libreoffice; do
59	        if have "$b"; then printf '%s\n' "$b"; return 0; fi
60	    done
61	    if [[ -x /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice ]]; then
62	        printf '%s\n' /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice
63	        return 0
64	    fi
65	    return 1
66	}
67	
68	# Render markdown from stdin: pretty ANSI via glow if present, else raw passthrough.
69	render_md() {
70	    if have glow; then
71	        glow -w "$WIDTH" -
72	    else
73	        cat
74	    fi
75	}
76	
77	render_docx() {
78	    local f="$1"
79	    need doxx "install via the devtools ansible role (brew bgreenwell/tap/doxx)"
80	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
81	        doxx --export ansi -w "$WIDTH" "$f"
82	    else
83	        doxx "$f"
84	    fi
85	}
86	
87	render_xlsx() {
88	    local f="$1"
89	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
90	        need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
91	        markitdown "$f" | render_md
92	    else
93	        need vd "install visidata via python_uv_tools (uv tool install visidata)"
94	        vd "$f"
95	    fi
96	}
97	
98	render_pptx() {
99	    local f="$1"
100	    need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
101	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
102	        markitdown "$f" | render_md
103	    elif have glow; then
104	        markitdown "$f" | glow -p -
105	    else
106	        markitdown "$f" | "${PAGER:-less}"
107	    fi
108	}
109	
110	# Legacy binary / OpenDocument formats: convert to the modern OOXML twin with
111	# LibreOffice headless (isolated -env profile so a running GUI instance doesn't
112	# lock us out), then re-dispatch. NOTE: we run the viewer as a child (no exec)
113	# so the EXIT trap still fires and cleans the tmpdir after an interactive TUI.
114	render_legacy() {
115	    local f="$1" target="$2" so tmp stem twin
116	    so="$(soffice_bin)" || {
117	        err "LibreOffice (soffice) not found — install via the devtools role (brew --cask libreoffice / apt libreoffice)"
118	        exit 2
119	    }
120	    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
121	    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
122	    if ! "$so" --headless -env:UserInstallation="file://$tmp/profile" \
123	            --convert-to "$target" --outdir "$tmp" "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
124	        err "LibreOffice failed to convert $f → $target"
125	        exit 1
126	    fi
127	    stem="$(basename -- "$f")"; stem="${stem%.*}"
128	    twin="$tmp/$stem.$target"
129	    [[ -f "$twin" ]] || { err "converted file not found: $twin"; exit 1; }
130	    render "$twin"
131	}
132	
133	render() {
134	    local f="$1" ext
135	    ext="${f##*.}"
136	    ext="$(printf '%s' "$ext" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"  # bash 3.2-safe lowercasing
137	    case "$ext" in
138	        docx)        render_docx "$f" ;;
139	        xlsx)        render_xlsx "$f" ;;
140	        pptx)        render_pptx "$f" ;;
141	        doc|odt|rtf) render_legacy "$f" docx ;;
142	        xls|ods)     render_legacy "$f" xlsx ;;
143	        ppt|odp)     render_legacy "$f" pptx ;;
144	        *)
145	            err "unsupported file type: .$ext"
146	            err "supported: docx xlsx pptx doc xls ppt odt ods odp rtf"
147	            exit 2
148	            ;;
149	    esac
150	}
151	
152	main() {
153	    local file=""
154	    while (($#)); do
155	        case "$1" in
156	            -p|--preview) PREVIEW=1; shift ;;
157	            -w|--width)
158	                [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { err "--width requires a value"; exit 2; }
159	                WIDTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
160	            --width=*) WIDTH="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
161	            -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
162	            --) shift; while (($#)); do file="$1"; shift; done; break ;;
163	            -*) err "unknown option: $1"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
164	            *)
165	                if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then file="$1"; else err "too many files: $1"; exit 2; fi
166	                shift ;;
167	        esac
168	    done
169	
170	    if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then
171	        err "expected a FILE"
172	        usage >&2
173	        exit 2
174	    fi
175	    if [[ ! -r "$file" ]]; then
176	        err "file not readable: $file"
177	        exit 1
178	    fi
179	    render "$file"
180	}
181	
182	main "$@"
183

139	# === Target Python interpreter override (CentOS 7 + similar) ===
140	#
141	# ansible-core 2.18+ modules wrap themselves in `from __future__ import
142	# annotations` (Py3.7+ syntax). When ansible runs against a target whose
143	# auto-discovered `/usr/bin/python3` is older (CentOS 7 ships 3.6.8),
144	# every task fails at the Gathering Facts stage with:
145	#   SyntaxError: future feature annotations is not defined
146	#
147	# Detect the auto-discovered python's version; if < 3.7, fall back to
148	# uv's managed python (already pulled into ~/.local/share/uv/python/...
149	# by `uv tool install ansible-core` in bootstrap) and pass it via
150	# -e ansible_python_interpreter. This is forward-compatible: on Rocky 9
151	# (Py 3.9+) the override is unnecessary and the if-branch is skipped.
152	#
153	# See pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md → "controller Python pin" for the
154	# matching controller-side fix; this is the target-side companion.
155	ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP=""
156	detect_target_python() {
157	    local sys_py="${1:-/usr/bin/python3}"
158	    if ! [[ -x "$sys_py" ]]; then
159	        return 1
160	    fi
161	    local sys_ver
162	    sys_ver="$("$sys_py" -c 'import sys; print(f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}")' 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
163	    # Pure-bash version comparison: Python is fine if >= 3.7
164	    awk -v v="$sys_ver" 'BEGIN { split(v, a, "."); exit !(a[1]>3 || (a[1]==3 && a[2]>=7)) }'
165	}
166	if ! detect_target_python; then
167	    # Find a Python 3.10+ via uv (controller used --python 3.13 by bootstrap).
168	    # Search uv's managed python dir + falls back to `uv python find` if uv is on PATH.
169	    UV_PY_CANDIDATE=""
170	    for cand in "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.13.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
171	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
172	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.11.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
173	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.10.*-linux-*/bin/python3; do
174	        if [[ -x "$cand" ]]; then
175	            UV_PY_CANDIDATE="$cand"
176	            break
177	        fi
178	    done
179	    if [[ -z "$UV_PY_CANDIDATE" ]] && command -v uv &> /dev/null; then
180	        UV_PY_CANDIDATE="$(uv python find 3.13 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.12 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.11 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.10 2>/dev/null)"
181	    fi
182	    if [[ -n "$UV_PY_CANDIDATE" && -x "$UV_PY_CANDIDATE" ]]; then
183	        ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP="$UV_PY_CANDIDATE"
184	        info "System python3 < 3.7; using uv-managed Python at $ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP"
185	    else
186	        warn "System python3 < 3.7 and no uv-managed python found; ansible Gathering Facts may fail"
187	        warn "Manual fallback: \`uv python install 3.13 && chezmoi apply\`"
188	    fi
189	fi

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# view-ebook — preview / open e-book formats that pandoc can't read: Kindle
# `.mobi` / `.azw` / `.azw3` (and `.fb2` / `.lit` / `.pdb` / `.prc`). EPUB is
# handled elsewhere (pandoc → full text); this covers the DRM-free formats
# calibre understands.
#
# Two modes (mirrors view-office):
#   view-ebook FILE              open in calibre's ebook-viewer (GUI) if present
#   view-ebook --preview FILE    metadata (title/author/description) to stdout
#
# There is no fast headless way to render mobi/azw *text*, so --preview shows
# rich metadata via calibre's `ebook-meta` (title, author, tags, description) —
# a "book back-cover" glance, the same philosophy as the SQLite table-listing
# preview. calibre's CLIs aren't on PATH from its macOS .app, so resolve the
# bundled binary the way view-office resolves LibreOffice's `soffice`.
#
# The yazi previewer contract (dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml) is:
#   run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"'
# See docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
set -euo pipefail

PREVIEW=0
WIDTH="${COLUMNS:-100}"

usage() {
    printf '%s\n' \
        "Usage: view-ebook [--preview] [--width N] FILE" \
        "" \
        "Preview or open an e-book (.mobi/.azw/.azw3/.fb2/.lit/.pdb/.prc)." \
        "" \
        "Options:" \
        "  -p, --preview    Print metadata (title/author/description) to stdout." \
        "  -w, --width N    Wrap width for --preview (default: \$COLUMNS or 100)." \
        "  -h, --help       Show this help." \
        "" \
        "Needs calibre (ebook-meta / ebook-viewer). EPUB is handled by pandoc, not here."
}

err() { printf 'view-ebook: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

# Resolve a calibre CLI ($1 = ebook-meta / ebook-viewer): PATH first, else the
# macOS .app bundle (the cask does not put calibre's binaries on PATH), else the
# common Linux install prefix.
calibre_bin() {
    local t="$1" b
    if command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1; then command -v "$t"; return 0; fi
    for b in "/Applications/calibre.app/Contents/MacOS/$t" \
             "/opt/calibre/$t" "/usr/bin/$t"; do
        [[ -x "$b" ]] && { printf '%s\n' "$b"; return 0; }
    done
    return 1
}

CALIBRE_HINT="install calibre — macOS: brew install --cask calibre (or enable the installCalibre prompt); Linux: apt install calibre"

render_preview() {
    local f="$1" em
    em="$(calibre_bin ebook-meta)" || { err "ebook-meta not found — $CALIBRE_HINT"; exit 2; }
    # ebook-meta prints an aligned "Field : value" block; the Comments/description
    # field carries HTML → strip tags for a readable preview. Cap the length.
    "$em" "$f" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/<[^>]+>//g' | head -n 200
}

open_interactive() {
    local f="$1" ev
    if ev="$(calibre_bin ebook-viewer)"; then
        exec "$ev" "$f"
    fi
    # No GUI viewer — fall back to metadata through a pager.
    err "calibre ebook-viewer not found; showing metadata instead ($CALIBRE_HINT)"
    render_preview "$f" | "${PAGER:-less}"
}

main() {
    local file=""
    while (($#)); do
        case "$1" in
            -p|--preview) PREVIEW=1; shift ;;
            -w|--width)
                [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { err "--width requires a value"; exit 2; }
                WIDTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --width=*) WIDTH="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
            -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
            --) shift; while (($#)); do file="$1"; shift; done; break ;;
            -*) err "unknown option: $1"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
            *)
                if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then file="$1"; else err "too many files: $1"; exit 2; fi
                shift ;;
        esac
    done

    [[ -n "$file" ]] || { err "expected a FILE"; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    [[ -r "$file" ]] || { err "file not readable: $file"; exit 1; }

    if ((PREVIEW)); then
        render_preview "$file"
    else
        open_interactive "$file"
    fi
}

main "$@"

```

# 56_view_ebook_completion.zsh - tab completion for `view-ebook`.
# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-ebook. Mirrors the bash twin
# 56_view_ebook_completion.bash — keep both in sync. See docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md §F.

}

compdef _view_ebook view-ebook

# 56_view_ebook_completion.bash - tab completion for `view-ebook`.
# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-ebook.
# Mirrors dot_config/zsh/tools/56_view_ebook_completion.zsh — keep both in sync.

_view_ebook_completion() {
    local cur prev words cword

    case "$prev" in
        -w|--width) return ;;

        -*)

            _filedir '@(mobi|azw|azw3|fb2|lit|pdb|prc|MOBI|AZW|AZW3|FB2|LIT|PDB|PRC)'
            ;;
    esac
}

complete -F _view_ebook_completion view-ebook

```text
1	# Yazi Preview Coverage
2	
3	Maximize what the [yazi](tmux/README.md) file manager can preview on hover — **images, PDF, video,
4	SVG, archives, ebooks, dmg**, on top of the tabular/office stacks documented in
5	[data-viewers.md](data-viewers.md) and [office-viewers.md](office-viewers.md).
6	
7	The catch: yazi's **built-in** previewers (images / PDF / video / SVG / standard archives) are *not*
8	wired in `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` — yazi ships them internally and **shells out to external
9	binaries at runtime**. If those binaries aren't installed, the hover pane shows an error
10	(`failed to spawn chafa`) or bare file-type classification. So "expanding coverage" is mostly a
11	**tool-install** job (a few ansible-managed binaries), plus two tiny config rules for the container
12	formats yazi ignores by default.
13	
14	## TL;DR — coverage matrix
15	
16	| File type | Preview | Powered by | Tier |
17	|---|---|---|---|
18	| png / jpg / webp / gif / bmp | image (or unicode-art) | yazi built-in → **chafa** to display | baseline |
19	| **PDF** | first page as image | yazi built-in → **poppler** (`pdftoppm`) + chafa | baseline |
20	| **SVG** | rendered image | yazi built-in → **resvg** + chafa | baseline |
21	| archives: zip / tar / gz / 7z / rar (+ zip-based apk / jar / whl / xpi) | file listing | yazi built-in → **7-Zip** | baseline |
22	| **dmg** | file listing | piper → **7-Zip** (`*.dmg` rule) | baseline |
23	| **EPUB** | text | piper → **pandoc** (`*.epub` rule) | baseline |
24	| video: mp4 / mkv / mov … | thumbnail | yazi built-in → **ffmpeg** + chafa | media (gated) |
25	| HEIC / JPEG-XL / fonts | image / sample | yazi built-in → **ImageMagick ≥7.1.1** + chafa | media (gated) |
26	| csv / tsv / parquet / xlsx / db / sqlite / feather | table | duckdb.yazi + fallbacks | plugin — see [data-viewers.md](data-viewers.md) |
27	| docx / pptx / legacy / ODF | rendered text | view-office (doxx / markitdown / LibreOffice) | plugin — see [office-viewers.md](office-viewers.md) |
28	| txt / json / md / source | text (+ syntax) | yazi built-in / `bat` | always |
29	
30	- **Baseline** tools are installed unconditionally by the `devtools` role (next to yazi).
31	- **Media (gated)** tools live in the `media_tools` role behind the `installMediaTools` prompt
32	  (default **off**; forced off on server/minimal). Video + HEIC previews work only where you opted in.
33	
34	## Why images showed `failed to spawn chafa`
35	
36	Every image-derived preview funnels through the same final **display** step. yazi renders png (direct),
37	PDF (via poppler), video (via ffmpeg), HEIC (via ImageMagick), SVG (via resvg) all *to an image*, then
38	hands that image to the display adapter it auto-selected. yazi picks the adapter from your terminal:
39	Kitty graphics protocol, iTerm2 inline, Sixel, Überzug++ (X11/Wayland), and — when none of those is
40	available (a non-graphics terminal, or inside tmux without passthrough) — **chafa**, its documented
41	*"last fallback resort"* that draws the image as Unicode/ANSI art.
42	
43	So a missing `chafa` breaks **all** of png/pdf/mp4/HEIC at once, even though poppler/ffmpeg/magick are
44	present — they produce the image fine; nothing can display it. Installing `chafa` fixes the whole set.
45
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
64	queries (chafa ≥1.16 probes on every render), with the escape framing stripped. Inside a multiplexer
65	(tmux / zellij) chafa often exits before the mux delivers the reply, so the mux hands the `rgb:…` bytes
66	to whatever now owns the tty — yazi — which reads them as keystrokes and opens a prompt. Upstream calls
67	this a multiplexer bug: [yazi #3680](https://github.com/sxyazi/yazi/issues/3680) (closed *not planned*),
68	[zellij #5138](https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/issues/5138) (same class). It bites hardest in
69	terminals with **no native graphics protocol** (e.g. Alacritty), where yazi must use chafa.
70	
71	**Fix (in this repo):** a `chafa` wrapper at `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_chafa` (→ `~/.dotfiles/bin/chafa`,
72	which precedes brew on `PATH`) forces **`--probe off`** — chafa never sends the query, so nothing leaks.
73	yazi hardcodes the bare `chafa` call with no way to pass flags, so shadowing the binary is the only
74	lever. `--probe off` merely disables color auto-detection (chafa falls back to `$TERM`/`$COLORTERM`
75	defaults; previews look the same), and the shim is **inert on graphics terminals** (yazi never calls
76	chafa there). Caveat: launch yazi from a configured shell so `~/.dotfiles/bin` is on `PATH`.
77	
78	## The two config rules (EPUB + dmg)
79	
80	Everything above except EPUB and dmg is pure tool-install — yazi's built-ins handle the routing. Those
81	two container mimes (`application/epub+zip`, `application/x-apple-diskimage`) are **not** in yazi's
82	built-in archive set, so `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` adds them via [`piper.yazi`](office-viewers.md#the-ya-pkg-plugin-mechanism):
83	
84	```toml
85	{ url = "*.epub", run = 'piper -- pandoc -f epub -t plain "$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
86	{ url = "*.dmg",  run = 'piper -- ( 7zz l "$1" 2>/dev/null || 7z l "$1" 2>/dev/null ) | head -n 200' },
87	```
88	
89	- `2>/dev/null` is **load-bearing** — piper renders any stderr as an error preview.
90	- `7zz || 7z` covers macOS `sevenzip` (`7zz`) vs Linux `p7zip-full` (`7z`).
91	- **No rule needed** for `.zip` / `.tar.*` / `.7z` / `.rar` or zip-based `.apk` / `.jar` / `.whl` /
92	  `.xpi` — yazi's built-in archive previewer lists them for free once 7-Zip is installed.
93	
94	## Per-OS install
95	
96	| Tool | macOS (brew, `devtools`) | Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) | Enables |
97	|---|---|---|---|
98	| **chafa** | `chafa` | apt `chafa` | image display fallback (all image-derived previews) |
99	| **poppler** | `poppler` | apt `poppler-utils` | PDF |
100	| **7-Zip** | `sevenzip` (`7zz`) | apt `p7zip-full` (`7z`) | archives + dmg |
101	| **resvg** | `resvg` | Linuxbrew → `cargo install resvg` (no apt pkg; non-fatal if absent) | SVG |
102	| ffmpeg | `ffmpeg` (`media_tools`, gated) | apt `ffmpeg` (gated) | video thumbnails |
103	| ImageMagick | `imagemagick` (`media_tools`, gated) | apt `imagemagick` (gated) | HEIC / JPEG-XL / fonts |
104	| pandoc | `pandoc` (already in `devtools`) | apt `pandoc` | EPUB text |
105	
106	## Gotchas
107	
108	- **Rename / shell popup with `rgb:…` junk on image hover** → the chafa OSC-query leak under
109	  tmux/zellij; fixed here by the `--probe off` shim — see [above](#chafa-probe-leak).
110	- **Ubuntu ImageMagick is v6.** apt ships ImageMagick 6 (no unified `magick`; weak HEIC), so HEIC/font
111	  previews may not work on Ubuntu even with `installMediaTools=true`. yazi wants **≥7.1.1**; v7 needs a
112	  PPA or source build (out of scope). macOS brew ImageMagick is v7 → fine.
113	- **Video/HEIC need `installMediaTools`.** ffmpeg + ImageMagick are opt-in. If mp4 thumbnails or HEIC
114	  previews are blank, re-run init with `installMediaTools=true` (or install ffmpeg/imagemagick by
115	  hand). Everything else in the baseline works without it.
116	- **resvg on Linux is best-effort.** No apt package → the role tries Linuxbrew then a one-time
117	  `cargo install resvg`. If neither is available, SVG simply previews as raw text — non-fatal.
118	- **Lowercase globs.** The `*.epub` / `*.dmg` rules match lowercase extensions; `Book.EPUB` won't fire
```
</details></tool-use>

120	
121	## Gotchas
122	
123	- **Rename / shell popup with `rgb:…` junk on image hover** → the chafa OSC-query leak under
124	  tmux/zellij; fixed here by the `--probe off` shim — see [above](#chafa-probe-leak).
125	- **Ubuntu ImageMagick is v6.** apt ships ImageMagick 6 (no unified `magick`; weak HEIC), so HEIC/font
126	  previews may not work on Ubuntu even with `installMediaTools=true`. yazi wants **≥7.1.1**; v7 needs a
127	  PPA or source build (out of scope). macOS brew ImageMagick is v7 → fine.
128	- **Video/HEIC need `installMediaTools`.** ffmpeg + ImageMagick are opt-in. If mp4 thumbnails or HEIC
129	  previews are blank, re-run init with `installMediaTools=true` (or install ffmpeg/imagemagick by
130	  hand). Everything else in the baseline works without it.
131	- **resvg on Linux is best-effort.** No apt package → the role tries Linuxbrew then a one-time
132	  `cargo install resvg`. If neither is available, SVG simply previews as raw text — non-fatal.
133	- **Lowercase globs.** The `*.epub` / `*.dmg` rules match lowercase extensions; `Book.EPUB` won't fire
134	  (yazi's built-ins are mime-based and unaffected).
135	- **chafa is a fallback, not a downgrade to avoid.** ascii-art is the correct behavior in a
136	  non-graphics terminal — see [above](#unicode-art-vs-crisp-inline-images).
137	
138	## Where things live
139	
140	| Surface | Path |
141	|---|---|
142	| Baseline tool install (chafa/poppler/7zip/resvg) | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
143	| chafa `--probe off` shim (fixes the rename/shell popup) | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_chafa` |
144	| Media tool install (ffmpeg/ImageMagick, gated) | `dot_ansible/roles/media_tools/tasks/main.yml` |
145	| EPUB + dmg previewer rules | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin] prepend_previewers` |
146	| yazi install | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (`# --- yazi ---`) |
147	| tmux image passthrough | `dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl` (`allow-passthrough on`) |
148	
149	## See also
150	
151	- [Data viewers](data-viewers.md) — the csv/parquet/xlsx/sqlite/feather table-preview stack (duckdb.yazi).
152	- [Office viewers](office-viewers.md) — the docx/pptx/legacy/ODF stack + the shared `ya pkg` / `piper.yazi` mechanism.
153	- [tool-managers.md § Tool index](../this_repo/tool-managers.md#tool-index-az) — where chafa / poppler / sevenzip / resvg come from per OS.
154	- yazi upstream: [installation deps](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/installation/), [image preview](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/image-preview/).

- What they control:

- Units / relation to pixels:

- Defaults:
  - No default values for "max_width" or "max_height" are provided in the excerpt above (defaults not shown).

- What causes an "Image size exceeds limit" error, and how max_width/max_height help:
  - Large images can be rejected when decoding if they exceed configured resource limits; the tasks options impose such limits: "image_alloc" (maximum memory allocation limit in bytes for decoding a single image, `0` for unlimited) and "image_bound" ("An array of `[width, height]`, maximum image size (in pixels) for decoding a single image, and `0` for unlimited"). Setting smaller "max_width" / "max_height" reduces the preview dimensions used and thereby lowers the chance the image will exceed decoding bounds or memory limits (and so helps avoid an "Image size exceeds limit" failure).

256	  { url = "*.azw3", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
257	  { url = "*.fb2", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# view-office — open or preview Microsoft Office / OpenDocument files in the
3	# terminal. Dispatches by extension to the right tool:
4	#   .docx → doxx        .xlsx → visidata (vd)   .pptx → markitdown | glow
5	#   (image-only .pptx → first embedded slide image via chafa; see render_pptx)
6	#   legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt/.odt/.ods/.odp/.rtf → LibreOffice headless converts to
7	#   the modern OOXML twin, then re-dispatches to the handler above.
8	#
9	# Two modes:
10	#   view-office FILE              interactive TUI / pager (default)
11	#   view-office --preview FILE    non-interactive ANSI/markdown to stdout
12	#
13	# Deliberately plain bash, NOT the `uv run --script` self-boot pattern used by
14	# executable_pqsum / yth / mlf: this sits on yazi's preview hot-path (invoked on
15	# every file hover via the piper.yazi previewer), where uv/Python startup
16	# (~100-200ms) would make previews feel laggy. Pure dispatch/exec is ~5ms.
17	#
18	# The yazi previewer contract (dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml) is:
19	#   run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"'
20	# Keep --preview/--width in sync with that. See docs/tools/office-viewers.md.
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	PREVIEW=0
24	WIDTH="${COLUMNS:-100}"
25	
26	usage() {
27	    printf '%s\n' \
28	        "Usage: view-office [--preview] [--width N] FILE" \
29	        "" \
30	        "Open or preview an Office / OpenDocument file in the terminal." \
31	        "" \
32	        "Options:" \
33	        "  -p, --preview    Render to stdout (ANSI/markdown) instead of a TUI." \
34	        "  -w, --width N    Wrap width for --preview (default: \$COLUMNS or 100)." \
35	        "  -h, --help       Show this help." \
36	        "" \
37	        "Formats:" \
38	        "  .docx  doxx (interactive) / doxx --export ansi (preview)" \
39	        "  .xlsx  visidata vd (interactive) / markitdown | glow (preview)" \
40	        "  .pptx  markitdown | glow pager (interactive) / markitdown | glow (preview)" \
41	        "  .doc .xls .ppt .odt .ods .odp .rtf  LibreOffice → OOXML twin, then above"
42	}
43	
44	err() { printf 'view-office: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
45	
46	have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
47	
48	# need TOOL "install hint" — fail with an actionable message if TOOL is absent.
49	need() {
50	    have "$1" && return 0
51	    err "$1 not found — $2"
52	    exit 2
53	}
54	
55	# Resolve the LibreOffice headless binary: `soffice` / `libreoffice` on PATH,
56	# else the macOS .app bundle (the cask does not put soffice on PATH).
57	soffice_bin() {
58	    local b
59	    for b in soffice libreoffice; do
60	        if have "$b"; then printf '%s\n' "$b"; return 0; fi
61	    done
62	    if [[ -x /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice ]]; then
63	        printf '%s\n' /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice
64	        return 0
65	    fi
66	    return 1
67	}
68	
69	# Render markdown from stdin: pretty ANSI via glow if present, else raw passthrough.
70	render_md() {
71	    if have glow; then
72	        glow -w "$WIDTH" -
73	    else
74	        cat
75	    fi
76	}
77	
78	render_docx() {
79	    local f="$1"
80	    need doxx "install via the devtools ansible role (brew bgreenwell/tap/doxx)"
81	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
82	        doxx --export ansi -w "$WIDTH" "$f"
83	    else
84	        doxx "$f"
85	    fi
86	}
87	
88	render_xlsx() {
89	    local f="$1"
90	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
91	        need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
92	        markitdown "$f" | render_md
93	    else
94	        need vd "install visidata via python_uv_tools (uv tool install visidata)"
95	        vd "$f"
96	    fi
97	}
98	
99	# Render the first embedded slide image of a pptx (ppt/media/image*) with chafa.
100	# Used only as an image-only-deck fallback: markitdown extracts no text from decks
101	# whose slides are full-page pictures, so we show the actual first slide instead of
102	# a list of `![](imageN)` refs. FAST (~0.5s: unzip one entry + chafa) — a full
103	# LibreOffice slide render is tens of seconds on image-heavy decks (the exact case
104	# we hit here). Best-effort: non-zero if 7-Zip/chafa are absent or no image is found.
105	render_pptx_thumbnail() {
106	    local f="$1" z img
107	    have chafa || return 1
108	    z="$(command -v 7zz || command -v 7z || true)"
109	    [[ -n "$z" ]] || return 1
110	    img="$("$z" l -slt "$f" 2>/dev/null | awk -F' = ' '/^Path = ppt\/media\/image/{print $2}' | sort -V | head -1)"
111	    [[ -n "$img" ]] || return 1
112	    "$z" e -so "$f" "$img" 2>/dev/null | chafa --format symbols --size "${WIDTH}x" - 2>/dev/null || return 1
113	}
114	
115	# Cheaply classify a pptx as text vs image-only by peeking at the slide XML for a
116	# non-empty text run (`<a:t>…`) with 7-Zip — far faster than a full markitdown
117	# parse on a big image-heavy deck. Prints text | notext | unknown (no 7-Zip).
118	_pptx_text_state() {
119	    local f="$1" z
120	    z="$(command -v 7zz || command -v 7z || true)"
121	    [[ -n "$z" ]] || { printf 'unknown\n'; return; }
122	    if "$z" e -so "$f" 'ppt/slides/slide*.xml' 2>/dev/null | grep -q '<a:t>[^<]'; then
123	        printf 'text\n'
124	    else
125	        printf 'notext\n'
126	    fi
127	}
128	
129	render_pptx() {
130	    local f="$1"
131	    need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
132	    if ! ((PREVIEW)); then
133	        if have glow; then markitdown "$f" | glow -p -; else markitdown "$f" | "${PAGER:-less}"; fi
134	        return
135	    fi
136	    # Preview: prefer extracted text; render the first embedded slide image only
137	    # for image-only decks (markitdown would otherwise emit a list of ![](imageN)).
138	    case "$(_pptx_text_state "$f")" in
139	        text)
140	            markitdown "$f" | render_md ;;
141	        notext)
142	            render_pptx_thumbnail "$f" || markitdown "$f" | render_md ;;
143	        *)
144	            # No 7-Zip to peek — fall back to a full markitdown parse, then judge:
145	            # strip slide-number comments + image refs + whitespace; empty ⇒ thumbnail.
146	            local md text
147	            md="$(markitdown "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)"
148	            text="$(printf '%s' "$md" | sed -E 's/<!--[^>]*-->//g; s/!\[[^]]*\]\([^)]*\)//g' | tr -d '[:space:]')"
149	            if [[ -n "$text" ]]; then
150	                printf '%s\n' "$md" | render_md
151	            else
152	                render_pptx_thumbnail "$f" || printf '%s\n' "$md" | render_md
153	            fi
154	            ;;
155	    esac
156	}
157	
158	# Legacy binary / OpenDocument formats: convert to the modern OOXML twin with
159	# LibreOffice headless (isolated -env profile so a running GUI instance doesn't
160	# lock us out), then re-dispatch. NOTE: we run the viewer as a child (no exec)
161	# so the EXIT trap still fires and cleans the tmpdir after an interactive TUI.
162	render_legacy() {
163	    local f="$1" target="$2" so tmp stem twin
164	    so="$(soffice_bin)" || {
165	        err "LibreOffice (soffice) not found — install via the devtools role (brew --cask libreoffice / apt libreoffice)"
166	        exit 2
167	    }
168	    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
169	    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
170	    if ! "$so" --headless -env:UserInstallation="file://$tmp/profile" \
171	            --convert-to "$target" --outdir "$tmp" "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
172	        err "LibreOffice failed to convert $f → $target"
173	        exit 1
174	    fi
175	    stem="$(basename -- "$f")"; stem="${stem%.*}"
176	    twin="$tmp/$stem.$target"
177	    [[ -f "$twin" ]] || { err "converted file not found: $twin"; exit 1; }
178	    render "$twin"
179	}
180	
181	render() {
182	    local f="$1" ext
183	    ext="${f##*.}"
184	    ext="$(printf '%s' "$ext" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"  # bash 3.2-safe lowercasing
185	    case "$ext" in
186	        docx)        render_docx "$f" ;;
187	        xlsx)        render_xlsx "$f" ;;
188	        pptx)        render_pptx "$f" ;;
189	        doc|odt|rtf) render_legacy "$f" docx ;;
190	        xls|ods)     render_legacy "$f" xlsx ;;
191	        ppt|odp)     render_legacy "$f" pptx ;;
192	        *)
193	            err "unsupported file type: .$ext"
194	            err "supported: docx xlsx pptx doc xls ppt odt ods odp rtf"
195	            exit 2
196	            ;;
197	    esac
198	}
199	
200	main() {
201	    local file=""
202	    while (($#)); do
203	        case "$1" in
204	            -p|--preview) PREVIEW=1; shift ;;
205	            -w|--width)
206	                [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { err "--width requires a value"; exit 2; }
207	                WIDTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
208	            --width=*) WIDTH="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
209	            -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
210	            --) shift; while (($#)); do file="$1"; shift; done; break ;;
211	            -*) err "unknown option: $1"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
212	            *)
213	                if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then file="$1"; else err "too many files: $1"; exit 2; fi
214	                shift ;;
215	        esac
216	    done
217	
218	    if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then
219	        err "expected a FILE"
220	        usage >&2
221	        exit 2
222	    fi
223	    if [[ ! -r "$file" ]]; then
224	        err "file not readable: $file"
225	        exit 1
226	    fi
227	    render "$file"
228	}
229	
230	main "$@"
231

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# view-ebook — preview / open e-book formats that pandoc can't read: Kindle
3	# `.mobi` / `.azw` / `.azw3` (and `.fb2` / `.lit` / `.pdb` / `.prc`). EPUB is
4	# handled elsewhere (pandoc → full text); this covers the DRM-free formats
5	# calibre understands.
6	#
7	# Two modes (mirrors view-office):
8	#   view-ebook FILE              open in calibre's ebook-viewer (GUI) if present
9	#   view-ebook --preview FILE    metadata (title/author/description) to stdout
10	#
11	# There is no fast headless way to render mobi/azw *text*, so --preview shows
12	# rich metadata via calibre's `ebook-meta` (title, author, tags, description) —
13	# a "book back-cover" glance, the same philosophy as the SQLite table-listing
14	# preview. calibre's CLIs aren't on PATH from its macOS .app, so resolve the
15	# bundled binary the way view-office resolves LibreOffice's `soffice`.
16	#
17	# The yazi previewer contract (dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml) is:
18	#   run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"'
19	# See docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
20	set -euo pipefail
21	
22	PREVIEW=0
23	WIDTH="${COLUMNS:-100}"
24	
25	usage() {
26	    printf '%s\n' \
27	        "Usage: view-ebook [--preview] [--width N] FILE" \
28	        "" \
29	        "Preview or open an e-book (.mobi/.azw/.azw3/.fb2/.lit/.pdb/.prc)." \
30	        "" \
31	        "Options:" \
32	        "  -p, --preview    Print metadata (title/author/description) to stdout." \
33	        "  -w, --width N    Wrap width for --preview (default: \$COLUMNS or 100)." \
34	        "  -h, --help       Show this help." \
35	        "" \
36	        "Needs calibre (ebook-meta / ebook-viewer). EPUB is handled by pandoc, not here."
37	}
38	
39	err() { printf 'view-ebook: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
40	
41	# Resolve a calibre CLI ($1 = ebook-meta / ebook-viewer): PATH first, else the
42	# macOS .app bundle (the cask does not put calibre's binaries on PATH), else the
43	# common Linux install prefix.
44	calibre_bin() {
45	    local t="$1" b
46	    if command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1; then command -v "$t"; return 0; fi
47	    for b in "/Applications/calibre.app/Contents/MacOS/$t" \
48	             "/opt/calibre/$t" "/usr/bin/$t"; do
49	        [[ -x "$b" ]] && { printf '%s\n' "$b"; return 0; }
50	    done
51	    return 1
52	}
53	
54	CALIBRE_HINT="install calibre — macOS: brew install --cask calibre (or enable the installCalibre prompt); Linux: apt install calibre"
55	
56	render_preview() {
57	    local f="$1" em
58	    em="$(calibre_bin ebook-meta)" || { err "ebook-meta not found — $CALIBRE_HINT"; exit 2; }
59	    # ebook-meta prints an aligned "Field : value" block; the Comments/description
60	    # field carries HTML → strip tags, wrap the long description to the pane width,
61	    # and cap the length.
62	    "$em" "$f" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/<[^>]+>//g' | fold -s -w "$WIDTH" | head -n 200
63	}
64	
65	open_interactive() {
66	    local f="$1" ev
67	    if ev="$(calibre_bin ebook-viewer)"; then
68	        exec "$ev" "$f"
69	    fi
70	    # No GUI viewer — fall back to metadata through a pager.
71	    err "calibre ebook-viewer not found; showing metadata instead ($CALIBRE_HINT)"
72	    render_preview "$f" | "${PAGER:-less}"
73	}
74	
75	main() {
76	    local file=""
77	    while (($#)); do
78	        case "$1" in
79	            -p|--preview) PREVIEW=1; shift ;;
80	            -w|--width)
81	                [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { err "--width requires a value"; exit 2; }
82	                WIDTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
83	            --width=*) WIDTH="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
84	            -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
85	            --) shift; while (($#)); do file="$1"; shift; done; break ;;
86	            -*) err "unknown option: $1"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
87	            *)
88	                if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then file="$1"; else err "too many files: $1"; exit 2; fi
89	                shift ;;
90	        esac
91	    done
92	
93	    [[ -n "$file" ]] || { err "expected a FILE"; usage >&2; exit 2; }
94	    [[ -r "$file" ]] || { err "file not readable: $file"; exit 1; }
95	
96	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
97	        render_preview "$file"
98	    else
99	        open_interactive "$file"
100	    fi
101	}
102	
103	main "$@"

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# chafa wrapper — force `--probe off`.
3	#
4	# WHY: yazi's fallback image adapter shells out to `chafa` for terminals with no
5	# native graphics protocol (e.g. Alacritty) and there is no way to pass it flags.
6	# chafa >=1.16 probes the terminal for its fg/bg colors via OSC 10/11 queries;
7	# inside tmux/zellij chafa often exits before the multiplexer delivers the reply,
8	# so the terminal's `rgb:…` response leaks into yazi's input buffer and pops a
9	# spurious rename / shell prompt (yazi #3680 — closed "not planned": it's a mux
10	# leak; chafa's `--probe off` is the source-side cure). `--probe off` only skips
11	# color auto-detection (chafa falls back to sensible defaults from $TERM/
12	# $COLORTERM), so ascii-art previews are unchanged.
13	#
14	# INERT on graphics terminals (Ghostty/Kitty/iTerm2/…): yazi uses the native
15	# protocol there and never calls chafa, so this shim is a no-op cost. It lives on
16	# ~/.dotfiles/bin, which precedes brew on PATH (dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl).
17	# See docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
18	set -e
19	
20	# Resolve the REAL chafa (this shim's dir is never in the list → no recursion).
21	real=""
22	for c in /opt/homebrew/bin/chafa /usr/local/bin/chafa \
23	         /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/chafa "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/chafa" \
24	         /usr/bin/chafa; do
25	  [ -x "$c" ] && { real="$c"; break; }
26	done
27	if [ -z "$real" ]; then
28	  # Fallback: first `chafa` on PATH outside this wrapper's own directory.
29	  selfdir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
30	  IFS=:
31	  for d in $PATH; do
32	    [ "$d" = "$selfdir" ] && continue
33	    [ -x "$d/chafa" ] && { real="$d/chafa"; break; }
34	  done
35	  unset IFS
36	fi
37	[ -n "$real" ] || { echo "chafa (yazi shim): real chafa not found on PATH" >&2; exit 127; }
38	
39	# Drop any caller-supplied --probe (space- or =-form), then force it off.
40	args=()
41	skip=0
42	for a in "$@"; do
43	  [ "$skip" = 1 ] && { skip=0; continue; }
44	  case "$a" in
45	    --probe)   skip=1 ;;
46	    --probe=*) ;;
47	    *) args+=("$a") ;;
48	  esac
49	done
50	exec "$real" "${args[@]}" --probe off
51
