170	exec marimo edit --watch .
171	' -- %s1
172	""", block = true, desc = "Marimo (watch dir)" },
173	]
174	
175	# --- marimo sandbox：只給 .py 用，避免對 dir 亂套
176	marimo_py_sandbox = [
177	  { run = """sh -lc 'exec marimo edit --watch --sandbox "$1"' -- %s1 """, block = true, desc = "Marimo (watch + sandbox py)" },
178	]
179	
180	# -----------------------
181	# Previewers — three families this repo wires explicitly, via yazi plugins
182	# auto-installed by `ya pkg install` on chezmoi apply (lockfile:
183	# dot_config/yazi/package.toml; installer:
184	# .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl).
185	# NOTE: images / PDF / video / SVG / standard archives are handled by yazi's
186	# BUILT-IN previewers (not wired here); those shell out to chafa/poppler/7zip/
187	# resvg — plus ffmpeg/imagemagick when installMediaTools — installed by the
188	# devtools/media_tools ansible roles. See docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
189	#
190	#   1. DATA FILES → duckdb.yazi (run = "duckdb"): csv/tsv/parquet/xlsx/db/duckdb.
191	#      Native DuckDB table view; K toggles SUMMARIZE, H/L scroll columns (see
192	#      keymap.toml); init.lua runs the REQUIRED `require("duckdb"):setup{}`. Needs
193	#      the `duckdb` CLI (devtools role). Two gaps filled via piper below:
194	#        - .feather/.arrow  → DuckDB has no Arrow-IPC reader → visidata `fixed`.
195	#        - .sqlite/.sqlite3 → not in the plugin's extension_map → duckdb table list
196	#          (plain `.db` IS handled by the plugin: DuckDB auto-attaches SQLite).
197	#   2. OFFICE DOCS → piper.yazi piping the in-house `view-office` dispatcher
198	#      (doxx / markitdown / LibreOffice).
199	#   3. CONTAINERS / e-books yazi's built-ins skip → piper: .epub (pandoc text),
200	#      Kindle .mobi/.azw/.azw3/.fb2 (view-ebook → calibre metadata), and .dmg
201	#      (7-Zip listing) — none of these mimes are in the built-in archive set.
202	#
203	# CONTRACTS / gotchas:
204	#   - view-office entries must stay in sync with view-office's --preview/--width
205	#     interface (dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office).
206	#   - piper passes $w=width, $h=height, $1=file path and runs the string via
207	#     `sh -c` (pipes/redirects work). piper renders any STDERR as an error, so the
208	#     visidata/duckdb/pandoc/7z fallbacks MUST keep `2>/dev/null`.
209	#   - .xlsx PREVIEW is owned by duckdb.yazi here (first xlsx preview per machine
210	#     fetches DuckDB's `spatial` ext → needs network once). The `view-office` CLI
211	#     still previews xlsx via markitdown; only yazi's previewer moved.
212	# See docs/tools/data-viewers.md, docs/tools/office-viewers.md, docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
213	# -----------------------
214	[plugin]
215	prepend_previewers = [
216	  # --- Data files → duckdb.yazi (native table view) ---
217	  { url = "*.csv", run = "duckdb" },
218	  { url = "*.tsv", run = "duckdb" },
219	  { url = "*.parquet", run = "duckdb" },
220	  { url = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb" },
221	  { url = "*.db", run = "duckdb" },
222	  { url = "*.duckdb", run = "duckdb" },
223	  # --- Feather / Arrow → visidata `fixed` table (no DuckDB Arrow-IPC reader) ---
224	  { url = "*.feather", run = 'piper -- vd -b -f arrow "$1" -o - --save-filetype fixed 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
225	  { url = "*.arrow", run = 'piper -- vd -b -f arrow "$1" -o - --save-filetype fixed 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
226	  # --- SQLite by .sqlite/.sqlite3 name → duckdb table listing (plugin only maps .db) ---
227	  { url = "*.sqlite", run = 'piper -- duckdb -readonly "$1" -box -c "SELECT table_name, column_count AS cols FROM duckdb_tables() ORDER BY table_name" 2>/dev/null' },
228	  { url = "*.sqlite3", run = 'piper -- duckdb -readonly "$1" -box -c "SELECT table_name, column_count AS cols FROM duckdb_tables() ORDER BY table_name" 2>/dev/null' },
229	
230	  # --- Office / OpenDocument → view-office (piper). .xlsx handled by duckdb above. ---
231	  { url = "*.docx", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
232	  { url = "*.pptx", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
233	  # Legacy binary + OpenDocument (LibreOffice converts → re-dispatches)
234	  { url = "*.doc", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
235	  { url = "*.xls", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
236	  { url = "*.ppt", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
237	  { url = "*.odt", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
238	  { url = "*.ods", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
239	  { url = "*.odp", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
240	  { url = "*.rtf", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
241	
242	  # --- Containers yazi's built-in previewers skip → piper ---
243	  # EPUB (application/epub+zip) → pandoc plain text; .dmg (application/x-apple-
244	  # diskimage) → 7-Zip content listing. Both mimes are absent from yazi's built-in
245	  # archive set, so without these they show only file-type classification.
246	  # (.zip/.tar.*/.7z/.rar and zip-based .apk/.jar/.whl/.xpi ARE handled free by the
247	  # built-in archive previewer once 7-Zip is installed — no rule needed.)
248	  # 2>/dev/null is load-bearing (piper renders stderr as an error preview);
249	  # 7zz→macOS `sevenzip`, 7z→Linux `p7zip-full`. pandoc is a devtools-role tool.
250	  { url = "*.epub", run = 'piper -- pandoc -f epub -t plain "$1" 2>/dev/null | head -n 500' },
251	  # Kindle / calibre e-books (pandoc can't read these) → view-ebook: calibre
252	  # ebook-meta metadata (title/author/description). Best-effort — no preview if
253	  # calibre is absent. See the installCalibre prompt + docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
254	  { url = "*.mobi", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
255	  { url = "*.azw", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
256	  { url = "*.azw3", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
257	  { url = "*.fb2", run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
258	  { url = "*.dmg", run = 'piper -- ( 7zz l "$1" 2>/dev/null || 7z l "$1" 2>/dev/null ) | head -n 200' },
259	]
260	
261	# duckdb.yazi builds parquet scroll-caches in a preload step — it needs matching
262	# preloader rules for the tabular formats (NOT .db/.duckdb, which are not
263	# pre-cached; NOT the piper fallbacks). See the plugin README.
264	prepend_preloaders = [
265	  { url = "*.csv", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
266	  { url = "*.tsv", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
267	  { url = "*.parquet", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
268	  { url = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
269	]
270

```text
1	# Ghostty & cmux
2	
3	[Ghostty](https://ghostty.org/) is a fast, native terminal emulator. [cmux](https://cmux.dev/) is a lightweight macOS terminal built on Ghostty for managing AI coding agents. Both read the same config file.
4	
5	## Managed config
6	
7	This repo manages `~/.config/ghostty/config` (via `dot_config/ghostty/config`). cmux reads this file first (before `~/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config`).
8	
9	Key settings:
10	
11	- **`macos-option-as-alt = left`** — Left Option sends Meta/Esc+ so tmux `M-` keybindings work (theme switching `M-c`/`M-t`, layouts `M-1`..`M-5`, fine resize `M-h/j/k/l`). Right Option retains macOS compose behavior for accents and special characters.
12	- **`font-features = -calt, -liga, -dlig`** — Disables ligatures for code readability.
13	
14	> **Note**: Restart Ghostty/cmux after changing the config — it is read on launch, not hot-reloaded.
15	
16	Without `macos-option-as-alt`, macOS Option produces Unicode compose characters (e.g. `Option+c` → `ç`) instead of `Esc+c`, silently breaking all tmux Meta bindings. Alacritty and iTerm2 have their own equivalent settings (`window.option_as_alt` and Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+ respectively).
17	
18	## `xterm-ghostty` terminfo on remote hosts
19	
20	When you SSH into a fresh remote, `$TERM=xterm-ghostty` but the remote has no matching terminfo entry. Symptoms: broken line-drawing, garbled prompts, `clear`/`tput` failures, Neovim rendering glitches. This is especially visible on the first cmux/tmux SSH into a new box.
21	
22	### Option 1 — Ghostty built-in (recommended for interactive shells)
23	
24	> - [Shell Integration - Features](https://ghostty.org/docs/features/shell-integration#ssh-integration)
25	
26	Add to `~/.config/ghostty/config`:
27	
28	```ini
29	shell-integration-features = ssh-env,ssh-terminfo
30	```
31	
32	- `ssh-terminfo`: auto-installs `xterm-ghostty` on the remote the first time you `ssh` from an interactive shell with Ghostty shell integration loaded.
33	- `ssh-env`: forwards `COLORTERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` via `SendEnv`, and falls back to `TERM=xterm-256color` where needed. The remote `sshd_config` needs a matching `AcceptEnv` line for the forwarded vars to take effect.
34	
35	**Limitations**: only triggers from interactive shells with the Ghostty wrapper active. It does not cover `ssh` invoked inside tmux/cmux panes, from scripts, or from wrapper tools (`rsync`, `aws`, `gcloud`, …). For those, use the manual helper below.
36	
37	### Option 2 — manual helper (works everywhere)
38	
39	A zsh function `ghostty-ssh-terminfo` is defined in [`dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh).
40	
41	```bash
42	ghostty-ssh-terminfo <ssh-host>
43	```
44	
45	What it does:
46	
47	- Validates local `infocmp` and the `xterm-ghostty` entry exist.
48	- Pipes `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` into a **single** SSH call (no double password/MFA prompt).
49	- On the remote: probes for `tic`, creates `~/.terminfo`, and runs `TERMINFO="$HOME/.terminfo" tic -x -` — so no root/sudo needed.
50	- Suppresses only the harmless `older tic versions may treat the description field as an alias` warning (emitted by ncurses < 6.3). Real errors still surface and set a non-zero exit.
51	
52	Example:
53	
54	```bash
55	# First time connecting a new box from cmux/tmux
56	ghostty-ssh-terminfo remote
57	# → Installed xterm-ghostty terminfo on remote (in ~/.terminfo)
58	
59	# Verify
60	ssh remote 'infocmp xterm-ghostty >/dev/null && echo ok'
61	```
62	
63	### Smoke-test against `localhost`
64	
65	Yes — if `sshd` is running locally you can validate the function without touching a real remote:
66	
67	```bash
68	# Enable sshd (Linux)
69	sudo systemctl start ssh
70	# or macOS: System Settings → General → Sharing → Remote Login
71	
72	ghostty-ssh-terminfo localhost
73	```
74	
75	Caveats:
76	
77	- `localhost` already has your own `$HOME`, so this effectively writes to the *same* `~/.terminfo` your local shell reads. Useful as a wiring/error-path smoke test, not as a representative "fresh remote" check.
78	- If you already have the entry locally (which you do, otherwise `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` would fail), the install is a no-op overwrite — still exercises the full pipeline end-to-end.
79	- For a cleaner test, point at a container or a VM where `xterm-ghostty` is definitely missing.
80	
81	## Why the warning appears (and can't be fully fixed client-side)
82	
83	The `|`-separated long description in Ghostty's terminfo is interpreted as an extra alias by `tic` / ncurses prior to 6.3. The entry still installs correctly; the warning is cosmetic. The only real fix is upgrading ncurses on the remote.
84	
85	## See also
86	
87	- [tmux](tmux.md) — tmux config and keybindings (cmux runs on top of tmux).
88	- [sesh](../sesh.md) — session picker used in the tmux setup.
89
```
</details></tool-use>

102	# a list of `![](imageN)` refs. FAST (~0.5s: unzip one entry + chafa) — a full
103	# LibreOffice slide render is tens of seconds on image-heavy decks (the exact case

105	render_pptx_thumbnail() {

109	    [[ -n "$z" ]] || return 1

117	# parse on a big image-heavy deck. Prints text | notext | unknown (no 7-Zip).
118	_pptx_text_state() {
119	    local f="$1" z
120	    z="$(command -v 7zz || command -v 7z || true)"
121	    [[ -n "$z" ]] || { printf 'unknown\n'; return; }
122	    if "$z" e -so "$f" 'ppt/slides/slide*.xml' 2>/dev/null | grep -q '<a:t>[^<]'; then
123	        printf 'text\n'
124	    else

132	    if ! ((PREVIEW)); then

135	    fi
136	    # Preview: prefer extracted text; render the first embedded slide image only
137	    # for image-only decks (markitdown would otherwise emit a list of ![](imageN)).
138	    case "$(_pptx_text_state "$f")" in
139	        text)
140	            markitdown "$f" | render_md ;;
141	        notext)
142	            render_pptx_thumbnail "$f" || markitdown "$f" | render_md ;;
143	        *)
144	            # No 7-Zip to peek — fall back to a full markitdown parse, then judge:
145	            # strip slide-number comments + image refs + whitespace; empty ⇒ thumbnail.
146	            local md text
147	            md="$(markitdown "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)"
148	            text="$(printf '%s' "$md" | sed -E 's/<!--[^>]*-->//g; s/!\[[^]]*\]\([^)]*\)//g' | tr -d '[:space:]')"
149	            if [[ -n "$text" ]]; then
150	                printf '%s\n' "$md" | render_md
151	            else
152	                render_pptx_thumbnail "$f" || printf '%s\n' "$md" | render_md
153	            fi
154	            ;;
155	    esac
156	}

159	# LibreOffice headless (isolated -env profile so a running GUI instance doesn't
160	# lock us out), then re-dispatch. NOTE: we run the viewer as a child (no exec)
161	# so the EXIT trap still fires and cleans the tmpdir after an interactive TUI.
162	render_legacy() {
163	    local f="$1" target="$2" so tmp stem twin
164	    so="$(soffice_bin)" || {
165	        err "LibreOffice (soffice) not found — install via the devtools role (brew --cask libreoffice / apt libreoffice)"
166	        exit 2
167	    }
168	    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"

170	    if ! "$so" --headless -env:UserInstallation="file://$tmp/profile" \
171	            --convert-to "$target" --outdir "$tmp" "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
172	        err "LibreOffice failed to convert $f → $target"
173	        exit 1
174	    fi
175	    stem="$(basename -- "$f")"; stem="${stem%.*}"
176	    twin="$tmp/$stem.$target"
177	    [[ -f "$twin" ]] || { err "converted file not found: $twin"; exit 1; }
178	    render "$twin"
179	}
180	
181	render() {
182	    local f="$1" ext
183	    ext="${f##*.}"
184	    ext="$(printf '%s' "$ext" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"  # bash 3.2-safe lowercasing
185	    case "$ext" in
186	        docx)        render_docx "$f" ;;
187	        xlsx)        render_xlsx "$f" ;;
188	        pptx)        render_pptx "$f" ;;
189	        doc|odt|rtf) render_legacy "$f" docx ;;
190	        xls|ods)     render_legacy "$f" xlsx ;;
191	        ppt|odp)     render_legacy "$f" pptx ;;
192	        *)
193	            err "unsupported file type: .$ext"
194	            err "supported: docx xlsx pptx doc xls ppt odt ods odp rtf"
195	            exit 2
196	            ;;
197	    esac
198	}
199	
200	main() {

202	    while (($#)); do
203	        case "$1" in
204	            -p|--preview) PREVIEW=1; shift ;;
205	            -w|--width)

207	                WIDTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;

209	            -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
210	            --) shift; while (($#)); do file="$1"; shift; done; break ;;
211	            -*) err "unknown option: $1"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# view-ebook — preview / open e-book formats that pandoc can't read: Kindle
3	# `.mobi` / `.azw` / `.azw3` (and `.fb2` / `.lit` / `.pdb` / `.prc`). EPUB is
4	# handled elsewhere (pandoc → full text); this covers the DRM-free formats
5	# calibre understands.
6	#
7	# Two modes (mirrors view-office):
8	#   view-ebook FILE              open in calibre's ebook-viewer (GUI) if present
9	#   view-ebook --preview FILE    metadata (title/author/description) to stdout
10	#
11	# There is no fast headless way to render mobi/azw *text*, so --preview shows
12	# rich metadata via calibre's `ebook-meta` (title, author, tags, description) —
13	# a "book back-cover" glance, the same philosophy as the SQLite table-listing
14	# preview. calibre's CLIs aren't on PATH from its macOS .app, so resolve the
15	# bundled binary the way view-office resolves LibreOffice's `soffice`.
16	#
17	# The yazi previewer contract (dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml) is:
18	#   run = 'piper -- view-ebook --preview --width "$w" "$1"'
19	# See docs/tools/yazi-previews.md.
20	set -euo pipefail
21	
22	PREVIEW=0
23	WIDTH="${COLUMNS:-100}"
24	
25	usage() {
26	    printf '%s\n' \
27	        "Usage: view-ebook [--preview] [--width N] FILE" \
28	        "" \
29	        "Preview or open an e-book (.mobi/.azw/.azw3/.fb2/.lit/.pdb/.prc)." \
30	        "" \
31	        "Options:" \
32	        "  -p, --preview    Print metadata (title/author/description) to stdout." \
33	        "  -w, --width N    Wrap width for --preview (default: \$COLUMNS or 100)." \
34	        "  -h, --help       Show this help." \
35	        "" \
36	        "Needs calibre (ebook-meta / ebook-viewer). EPUB is handled by pandoc, not here."
37	}
38	
39	err() { printf 'view-ebook: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
40	
41	# Resolve a calibre CLI ($1 = ebook-meta / ebook-viewer): PATH first, else the
42	# macOS .app bundle (the cask does not put calibre's binaries on PATH), else the
43	# common Linux install prefix.
44	calibre_bin() {
45	    local t="$1" b
46	    if command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1; then command -v "$t"; return 0; fi
47	    for b in "/Applications/calibre.app/Contents/MacOS/$t" \
48	             "/opt/calibre/$t" "/usr/bin/$t"; do
49	        [[ -x "$b" ]] && { printf '%s\n' "$b"; return 0; }
50	    done
51	    return 1
52	}
53	
54	CALIBRE_HINT="install calibre — macOS: brew install --cask calibre (or enable the installCalibre prompt); Linux: apt install calibre"
55	
56	render_preview() {
57	    local f="$1" em
58	    em="$(calibre_bin ebook-meta)" || { err "ebook-meta not found — $CALIBRE_HINT"; exit 2; }
59	    # ebook-meta prints an aligned "Field : value" block; the Comments/description
60	    # field carries HTML → strip tags, wrap the long description to the pane width,
61	    # and cap the length.
62	    "$em" "$f" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/<[^>]+>//g' | fold -s -w "$WIDTH" | head -n 200
63	}
64	
65	open_interactive() {
66	    local f="$1" ev
67	    if ev="$(calibre_bin ebook-viewer)"; then
68	        exec "$ev" "$f"
69	    fi
70	    # No GUI viewer — fall back to metadata through a pager.
71	    err "calibre ebook-viewer not found; showing metadata instead ($CALIBRE_HINT)"
72	    render_preview "$f" | "${PAGER:-less}"
73	}
74	
75	main() {
76	    local file=""
77	    while (($#)); do
78	        case "$1" in
79	            -p|--preview) PREVIEW=1; shift ;;
80	            -w|--width)
81	                [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { err "--width requires a value"; exit 2; }
82	                WIDTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
83	            --width=*) WIDTH="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
84	            -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
85	            --) shift; while (($#)); do file="$1"; shift; done; break ;;
86	            -*) err "unknown option: $1"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
87	            *)
88	                if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then file="$1"; else err "too many files: $1"; exit 2; fi
89	                shift ;;
90	        esac
91	    done
92	
93	    [[ -n "$file" ]] || { err "expected a FILE"; usage >&2; exit 2; }
94	    [[ -r "$file" ]] || { err "file not readable: $file"; exit 1; }
95	
96	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
97	        render_preview "$file"
98	    else
99	        open_interactive "$file"
100	    fi
101	}
102	
103	main "$@"

  - Preview options (max_width, max_height and other preview tuning) are configured under [preview] in yazi.toml. ([yazi-rs.github.io](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/image-preview/))

  - max_width and max_height control the maximum preview dimensions (in pixels) Yazi uses for image pre-caching and preview scaling. Default max_width is 600 (unless changed). ([deepwiki.com](https://deepwiki.com/yazi-rs/yazi-rs.github.io/3.1-yazi.toml-reference))

- What image_alloc and image_bound do
  - Under [tasks], image_alloc sets the maximum memory (bytes) Yazi will allocate when decoding a single image (0 = unlimited). image_bound is [width, height] — the maximum image size in pixels that Yazi will decode (0 = unlimited). ([yazi-rs.github.io](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/yazi/))

- The “Image size exceeds limit” error and related threads
  - Issues and discussions in the Yazi repo show that the “Image size exceeds limit” message appears when an image exceeds the configured bounds and users resolved it by increasing image_bound or image_alloc (or setting to 0 for unlimited), or by changing preview/ueberzug scaling. - Practical troubleshooting / fixes (reported by users)
  - Increase [tasks].image_bound (e.g. larger width/height) or set to [0, 0] to disable the pixel bound. ([yazi-rs.github.io](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/yazi/))
  - Increase [tasks].image_alloc (bytes) if decoding large images hits memory limits (default is 512 MiB). ([deepwiki.com](https://deepwiki.com/yazi-rs/yazi-rs.github.io/3.1-yazi.toml-reference))

253	local function get_cache_path(job, mode, extension)
254		local suffix = "_" .. mode .. ".parquet"
255		if extension then
256			suffix = "_" .. extension .. "." .. extension
257		end
258		local cache_version = 3
259		local skip = job.skip
260		job.skip = 1000000 + cache_version
261		local base = ya.file_cache(job)
262		job.skip = skip
263	
264		if not base then
265			return nil, nil
266		end
267	
268		local base_str = tostring(base) .. suffix
269		local path_url = Url(base_str)
270		local path_str = tostring(path_url.name)
271		return path_str, path_url
272	end

276		local width = math.max((job.area and job.area.w * 3 or 80), 80)
277		local height = math.max((job.area and job.area.h or 25), 25)
278	
279		local args = {}
280	
281		if file_type == "duckdb" then
282			table.insert(args, "-readonly")
283			table.insert(args, tostring(target))
284		elseif file_type == "excel" then
285			add_queries_to_table(args, { "install spatial", "load spatial" })
286		end

293			string.format(".maxwidth %d", width),
294			string.format(".maxrows %d", height),
295			".highlight_results on",
296		})
297	
298		-- Add query or list of queries

300	
301		local child = Command("duckdb"):arg(args):stdout(Command.PIPED):stderr(Command.PIPED):spawn()
302		if not child then
303			ya.err("Failed to spawn DuckDB")

308		if err or not output.status.success then

310			return nil
311		end

314	end

316	local function generate_db_query(limit, offset)
317		local scroll = get_opts("scrolled_columns") or 0
318	
319		local metadata_fields = { "rows", "columns", "has_pk", "indexes" }
320		local visible_column_count = 10
321		local max_scroll_metadata = #metadata_fields
322		local metadata_projection = { "table_name" }
323	
324		if scroll < max_scroll_metadata then
325			for i = scroll + 1, #metadata_fields do
326				table.insert(metadata_projection, metadata_fields[i])
327			end
328			table.insert(metadata_projection, "column_names") -- always show
329	
330			local projection = table.concat(metadata_projection, ", ")
331			return string.format(
332				[[
333	WITH table_info AS (
334	  SELECT
335	    DISTINCT t.table_name,
336	    t.estimated_size AS rows,
337	    t.column_count AS columns,
338	    t.has_primary_key AS has_pk,
339	    t.index_count AS indexes,
340	    STRING_AGG(c.column_name, ', ' ORDER BY c.column_index) OVER (PARTITION BY t.table_name) AS column_names
341	  FROM duckdb_tables() t
342	  LEFT JOIN duckdb_columns() c ON t.table_name = c.table_name
343	)
344	SELECT %s FROM table_info
345	ORDER BY table_name
346	LIMIT %d OFFSET %d;
347	]],
348				projection,
349				limit,
350				offset
351			)
352		else
353			local column_scroll = scroll - max_scroll_metadata
354			local start_pos = column_scroll + 1
355			local end_pos = column_scroll + visible_column_count
356	
357			return string.format(
358				[[
359	WITH raw AS (
360	  SELECT
361	    t.table_name,
362	    c.column_name,
363	    row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY t.table_name ORDER BY c.column_index) AS col_pos
364	  FROM duckdb_tables() t
365	  LEFT JOIN duckdb_columns() c ON t.table_name = c.table_name
366	),
367	scrolling AS (
368	  SELECT
369	    table_name,
370	    column_name,
371	    col_pos
372	  FROM raw
373	  WHERE col_pos >= %d AND col_pos < %d
374	),
375	aggregated AS (
376	  SELECT
377	    table_name,
378	    STRING_AGG(column_name, ', ' ORDER BY col_pos) AS column_names
379	  FROM scrolling
380	  GROUP BY table_name
381	)
382	SELECT table_name, column_names FROM aggregated
383	ORDER BY table_name
384	LIMIT %d OFFSET %d;
385	]],
386				start_pos,
387				end_pos,
388				limit,
389				offset
390			)
391		end
392	end

729	function M:preload(job)
730		if is_plain_text(job, nil) then

751	-- Peek with mode toggle if scrolling at top
752	function M:peek(job)
753		local args = prepare_peek_context(job)
754		if is_plain_text(job, args.file_type) then
755			return require("code"):peek(job)
756		end
757	
758		local query = generate_peek_query(args.target, job, args.limit, args.offset, args.file_type, args.cache_str)
759		ya.dbg("query: " .. tostring(query))
760		local output = run_query(job, query, args.target, args.file_type)

762		ya.dbg("stderr: " .. tostring(output.stderr))
763		if not output_is_valid(output, args.mode, job) then

768			elseif is_on_list("bad_cache", args.cache_str) then

770			end
771		end
772	
773		if args.target == args.file_url and args.mode == "summarized" and not args.use_cache then
774			render_output(output, job)
775			while not is_on_list("completed", args.cache_str) do

778			clear_list("completed")
779			set_opts("re_peek", true)
780			return require("duckdb"):peek(job)

784	end

797			set_opts("mode", new_mode)

So the issue is that when the metadata description gets long enough to exceed 200 lines after folding, `head -n 200` closes the pipe early and sends SIGPIPE to the upstream processes. With `pipefail` enabled, this causes the pipeline to return 141, and since `set -e` is active, the render_preview function exits with 141 even though the preview actually rendered successfully. The script then exits with that error code instead of succeeding.

It's a real but narrow bug—most books have descriptions that won't exceed 200 lines after folding, but some with lengthy reviews or comments could trigger it. The severity is low to medium since it's uncommon but would cause yazi's piper previewer to show an error despite the preview working fine.

The key point: when ebook-meta is absent, the pipeline never runs at all because the `calibre_bin` check fails first and exits with code 2. So the `set -euo pipefail` + fold/sed behavior question only applies when ebook-meta is present and the output is long enough to hit the head-SIGPIPE edge case. local M = {}

local function fail(job, s) ya.preview_widget(job, ui.Text.parse(s):area(job.area):wrap(ui.Wrap.YES)) end

function M:peek(job)
	local child, err = Command("sh")
		:arg({ "-c", job.args[1], "sh", tostring(job.file.path) })
		:env("w", job.area.w)
		:env("h", job.area.h)
		:env("t", rt.term.light and "light" or "dark")
		:env("CYGWIN", "noupcaseenv")
		:stdout(Command.PIPED)
		:stderr(Command.PIPED)
		:spawn()

	if not child then
		return fail(job, "sh: " .. err)
	end

	local limit = job.area.h
	local i, outs, errs = 0, {}, {}
	repeat
		local next, event = child:read_line()
		if event == 1 then
			errs[#errs + 1] = next
		elseif event ~= 0 then
			break
		end

		i = i + 1
		if i > job.skip then
			outs[#outs + 1] = next
		end
	until i >= job.skip + limit

	child:start_kill()
	if #errs > 0 then
		fail(job, table.concat(errs, ""))
	elseif job.skip > 0 and i < job.skip + limit then
		ya.emit("peek", { math.max(0, i - limit), only_if = job.file.url, upper_bound = true })
	else
		ya.preview_widget(job, M.format(job, outs))
	end
end

function M:seek(job) require("code"):seek(job) end

		return ui.Text.parse(s):area(job.area)

55	# Resolve the LibreOffice headless binary: `soffice` / `libreoffice` on PATH,
56	# else the macOS .app bundle (the cask does not put soffice on PATH).
57	soffice_bin() {
58	    local b
59	    for b in soffice libreoffice; do
60	        if have "$b"; then printf '%s\n' "$b"; return 0; fi
61	    done
62	    if [[ -x /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice ]]; then
63	        printf '%s\n' /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice
64	        return 0
65	    fi
66	    return 1
67	}
68	
69	# Render markdown from stdin: pretty ANSI via glow if present, else raw passthrough.
70	render_md() {
71	    if have glow; then
72	        glow -w "$WIDTH" -
73	    else
74	        cat
75	    fi
76	}
77	
78	render_docx() {
79	    local f="$1"
80	    need doxx "install via the devtools ansible role (brew bgreenwell/tap/doxx)"
81	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
82	        doxx --export ansi -w "$WIDTH" "$f"
83	    else
84	        doxx "$f"
85	    fi
86	}
87	
88	render_xlsx() {
89	    local f="$1"
90	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
91	        need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
92	        markitdown "$f" | render_md
93	    else
94	        need vd "install visidata via python_uv_tools (uv tool install visidata)"
95	        vd "$f"
96	    fi
97	}
98	
99	# Render the first embedded slide image of a pptx (ppt/media/image*) with chafa.
100	# Used only as an image-only-deck fallback: markitdown extracts no text from decks
101	# whose slides are full-page pictures, so we show the actual first slide instead of
102	# a list of `![](imageN)` refs. FAST (~0.5s: unzip one entry + chafa) — a full
103	# LibreOffice slide render is tens of seconds on image-heavy decks (the exact case
104	# we hit here). Best-effort: non-zero if 7-Zip/chafa are absent or no image is found.
105	render_pptx_thumbnail() {
106	    local f="$1" z img
107	    have chafa || return 1
108	    z="$(command -v 7zz || command -v 7z || true)"
109	    [[ -n "$z" ]] || return 1
110	    img="$("$z" l -slt "$f" 2>/dev/null | awk -F' = ' '/^Path = ppt\/media\/image/{print $2}' | sort -V | head -1)"
111	    [[ -n "$img" ]] || return 1
112	    "$z" e -so "$f" "$img" 2>/dev/null | chafa --format symbols --size "${WIDTH}x" - 2>/dev/null || return 1
113	}
114	
115	# Cheaply classify a pptx as text vs image-only by peeking at the slide XML for a
116	# non-empty text run (`<a:t>…`) with 7-Zip — far faster than a full markitdown
117	# parse on a big image-heavy deck. Prints text | notext | unknown (no 7-Zip).
118	_pptx_text_state() {
119	    local f="$1" z
120	    z="$(command -v 7zz || command -v 7z || true)"
121	    [[ -n "$z" ]] || { printf 'unknown\n'; return; }
122	    if "$z" e -so "$f" 'ppt/slides/slide*.xml' 2>/dev/null | grep -q '<a:t>[^<]'; then
123	        printf 'text\n'
124	    else
125	        printf 'notext\n'
126	    fi
127	}
128	
129	render_pptx() {
130	    local f="$1"
131	    need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
132	    if ! ((PREVIEW)); then
133	        if have glow; then markitdown "$f" | glow -p -; else markitdown "$f" | "${PAGER:-less}"; fi
134	        return
135	    fi
136	    # Preview: prefer extracted text; render the first embedded slide image only
137	    # for image-only decks (markitdown would otherwise emit a list of ![](imageN)).
138	    case "$(_pptx_text_state "$f")" in
139	        text)
140	            markitdown "$f" | render_md ;;
141	        notext)
142	            render_pptx_thumbnail "$f" || markitdown "$f" | render_md ;;
143	        *)
144	            # No 7-Zip to peek — fall back to a full markitdown parse, then judge:
145	            # strip slide-number comments + image refs + whitespace; empty ⇒ thumbnail.
146	            local md text
147	            md="$(markitdown "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)"
148	            text="$(printf '%s' "$md" | sed -E 's/<!--[^>]*-->//g; s/!\[[^]]*\]\([^)]*\)//g' | tr -d '[:space:]')"
149	            if [[ -n "$text" ]]; then
150	                printf '%s\n' "$md" | render_md
151	            else
152	                render_pptx_thumbnail "$f" || printf '%s\n' "$md" | render_md
153	            fi
154	            ;;
155	    esac
156	}
157	
158	# Legacy binary / OpenDocument formats: convert to the modern OOXML twin with
159	# LibreOffice headless (isolated -env profile so a running GUI instance doesn't
160	# lock us out), then re-dispatch. NOTE: we run the viewer as a child (no exec)
161	# so the EXIT trap still fires and cleans the tmpdir after an interactive TUI.
162	render_legacy() {
163	    local f="$1" target="$2" so tmp stem twin
164	    so="$(soffice_bin)" || {
165	        err "LibreOffice (soffice) not found — install via the devtools role (brew --cask libreoffice / apt libreoffice)"
166	        exit 2
167	    }
168	    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
169	    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
170	    if ! "$so" --headless -env:UserInstallation="file://$tmp/profile" \
171	            --convert-to "$target" --outdir "$tmp" "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
172	        err "LibreOffice failed to convert $f → $target"
173	        exit 1
174	    fi
175	    stem="$(basename -- "$f")"; stem="${stem%.*}"
176	    twin="$tmp/$stem.$target"
177	    [[ -f "$twin" ]] || { err "converted file not found: $twin"; exit 1; }
178	    render "$twin"
179	}
180	
181	render() {
182	    local f="$1" ext
183	    ext="${f##*.}"
184	    ext="$(printf '%s' "$ext" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"  # bash 3.2-safe lowercasing
185	    case "$ext" in
186	        docx)        render_docx "$f" ;;
187	        xlsx)        render_xlsx "$f" ;;
188	        pptx)        render_pptx "$f" ;;
189	        doc|odt|rtf) render_legacy "$f" docx ;;
190	        xls|ods)     render_legacy "$f" xlsx ;;
191	        ppt|odp)     render_legacy "$f" pptx ;;
192	        *)
193	            err "unsupported file type: .$ext"
194	            err "supported: docx xlsx pptx doc xls ppt odt ods odp rtf"
195	            exit 2
196	            ;;
197	    esac
198	}
199	
200	main() {
201	    local file=""
202	    while (($#)); do
203	        case "$1" in
204	            -p|--preview) PREVIEW=1; shift ;;
205	            -w|--width)
206	                [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { err "--width requires a value"; exit 2; }
207	                WIDTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
208	            --width=*) WIDTH="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
209	            -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
210	            --) shift; while (($#)); do file="$1"; shift; done; break ;;
211	            -*) err "unknown option: $1"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
212	            *)
213	                if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then file="$1"; else err "too many files: $1"; exit 2; fi
214	                shift ;;
215	        esac
216	    done
217	
218	    if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then
219	        err "expected a FILE"
220	        usage >&2
221	        exit 2
222	    fi
223	    if [[ ! -r "$file" ]]; then
224	        err "file not readable: $file"
225	        exit 1
226	    fi
227	    render "$file"
228	}
229	
230	main "$@"
231

```text
1	# View Office Documents in the Terminal
2	
3	Open and preview Microsoft Office (`.docx` / `.xlsx` / `.pptx`), legacy binary (`.doc` / `.xls` / `.ppt`), and OpenDocument (`.odt` / `.ods` / `.odp`) files without leaving the terminal — no Microsoft Office, no GUI.
4	
5	There is no single tool that views everything well, so this repo wires a small **per-format + two-mode** stack behind one dispatcher, [`view-office`](#the-view-office-dispatcher), and hooks it into the [yazi](tmux/README.md) file manager for inline previews.
6	
7	## TL;DR
8	
9	| Format | Interactive (TUI / pager) | Quick preview (stdout) |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| Word `.docx` | [`doxx`](https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx) | `doxx --export ansi` |
12	| Excel `.xlsx` | [`visidata`](https://www.visidata.org/) (`vd`) | `markitdown \| glow` |
13	| PowerPoint `.pptx` | `markitdown \| glow` (pager) | `markitdown \| glow`; image-only decks → slide-1 thumbnail (chafa) |
14	| Legacy `.doc/.xls/.ppt`, OpenDocument `.odt/.ods/.odp`, `.rtf` | LibreOffice → OOXML twin → above | same, converted first |
15	
16	```console
17	$ view-office report.docx                 # interactive: rich TUI (doxx)
18	$ view-office --preview budget.xlsx        # markdown/ANSI to stdout
19	$ view-office legacy-memo.doc              # LibreOffice converts, then doxx
20	```
21	
22	## The `view-office` dispatcher
23	
24	`view-office` (source: `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office`, deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/`, on `PATH`) is a small bash script that dispatches by file extension:
25	
26	```text
27	view-office [--preview] [--width N] FILE
28	  -p, --preview    render to stdout (ANSI/markdown) instead of launching a TUI
29	  -w, --width N    wrap width for --preview (default: $COLUMNS or 100)
30	  -h, --help       show help
31	```
32	
33	Two modes:
34	
35	- **Interactive** (default) — launches the best full-screen viewer for the type: `doxx` for Word, `visidata` for Excel, a `glow` pager for PowerPoint.
36	- **Preview** (`--preview`) — emits ANSI/markdown to stdout. This is the single source of truth that the [yazi previewer](#yazi-inline-previews) (and any future `tv` / `fzf` integration) calls, so preview logic lives in exactly one place.
37	
38	Legacy binary and OpenDocument formats are converted to their modern OOXML twin with **LibreOffice headless** into a temp dir, then re-dispatched to the handler above (e.g. `.doc → .docx → doxx`). Missing tools produce an actionable install hint and exit 2 — nothing fails silently.
39	
40	> **Why bash, not the `uv run --script` pattern** used by `pqsum`/`yth`/`mlf`? `view-office` sits on yazi's preview hot-path (invoked on every file hover). uv/Python startup (~100–200 ms) would make previews feel laggy; bash dispatch is ~5 ms.
41	
42	## The tools
43	
44	### doxx — terminal-native Word viewer
45	
46	[doxx](https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx) renders `.docx` directly in the terminal: bold/italic/headings, smart tables, LaTeX equations, and inline images (Kitty/iTerm2/Sixel). It also exports non-interactively — `doxx FILE --export ansi|markdown|text|csv|json` — which is what `view-office --preview` uses for Word.
47	
48	- **macOS:** `brew install doxx` (it's in **homebrew-core** — the README's `bgreenwell/tap/doxx` is stale; that tap ships `xleak`/`lstr`, not doxx).
49	- **Linux:** GitHub release `.tar.xz` (cargo-dist, static musl on x86_64) → `~/.local/bin/doxx`, installed by the `devtools` ansible role.
50	
51	### visidata — spreadsheet multitool
52	
53	Already in the repo (see [Data Viewers](../shells/aliases.md)). `vd file.xlsx` opens a fast, vim-keyed TUI over the sheet. Used for **interactive** Excel; for previews, `markitdown` renders the sheet to a markdown table instead (visidata is TUI-only).
54	
55	### markitdown — Office → Markdown
56	
57	[Microsoft MarkItDown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown) converts `.docx/.xlsx/.pptx` (and more) to Markdown, optimized for LLM/RAG pipelines. It is the universal preview engine for Excel and PowerPoint here, because **pandoc cannot read `.pptx` or `.xlsx`** (pandoc only *writes* pptx; it reads docx/odt/epub but not the spreadsheet/presentation formats). Installed as a uv tool (`python_uv_tools`).
58	
59	> **Gotcha:** the bare `markitdown` package ships **no format converters** — they live in optional extras. This repo installs `markitdown[docx,xlsx,pptx]`; without the extras every Office file raises `MissingDependencyException`. (Not `[all]` — that adds pdf/audio/youtube/azure bloat.)
60	
61	> **Image-only `.pptx`:** markitdown extracts *text*, so a deck whose slides are full-page images yields nothing but `![](imageN)` refs. For `--preview`, `view-office`'s `render_pptx` detects this by peeking at the slide XML with 7-Zip; if there's no text it extracts the first embedded slide image (`ppt/media/image1.*`) and renders it with [`chafa`](yazi-previews.md) — ~0.5 s, versus tens of seconds for a full LibreOffice slide render on image-heavy decks. Text decks still get the markitdown path.
62	
63	### LibreOffice — legacy-format fallback
64	
65	Only `soffice --headless --convert-to` can read the old binary formats (`.doc/.xls/.ppt`) and OpenDocument. Heavy (~hundreds of MB), so it's a **fallback**, installed by `devtools` (macOS cask / `libreoffice-writer,calc,impress` on Debian with recommends off). On macOS `soffice` is not on `PATH`; `view-office` resolves the `.app` bundle path itself. No-root Linux installs skip it and `view-office` prints an install hint for legacy files.
66	
67	## Yazi inline previews
68	
69	Hovering an Office file in [yazi](tmux/README.md) renders a preview in the right pane. This is the repo's first yazi **plugin** integration, via the [`ya pkg`](#the-ya-pkg-plugin-mechanism) manager and the [`piper.yazi`](https://github.com/yazi-rs/plugins/tree/main/piper.yazi) plugin ("pipe any shell command as a previewer"):
70	
71	```toml
72	# dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml
73	[plugin]
74	prepend_previewers = [
75	  { url = "*.docx", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
76	  # … .pptx .doc .xls .ppt .odt .ods .odp .rtf
77	]
78	```
79	
80	> **`.xlsx` preview is handled by [duckdb.yazi](data-viewers.md), not `view-office`.** Yazi routes
81	> spreadsheet hovers to the DuckDB table previewer (a nicer aligned grid). The
82	> `view-office --preview budget.xlsx` **CLI** path (markitdown → glow) is unchanged — only Yazi's
83	> previewer wiring moved. Legacy `.xls` / OpenDocument `.ods` stay on the view-office (LibreOffice)
84	> path here, since DuckDB can't read those.
85	
86	`piper.yazi` passes `$w` (preview width) and `$1` (file path); the command's stdout becomes the preview. The `run` string and `view-office`'s `--preview`/`--width` interface are a **contract** — change one, change the other.
87	
88	### The `ya pkg` plugin mechanism
89	
90	`ya pkg` is Yazi's plugin manager (`ya` is the CLI companion shipped with yazi). It clones a plugin, copies it into `~/.config/yazi/plugins/`, and locks its version in `~/.config/yazi/package.toml`.
91	
92	In this repo the lockfile is **chezmoi-managed** (`dot_config/yazi/package.toml`) and the plugins are materialized by a hash-gated run-script:
93	
94	| Piece | Path | Role |
95	|---|---|---|
96	| Lockfile (SSOT) | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml` | pins `yazi-rs/plugins:piper` (rev + hash) |
97	| Installer | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` | runs `ya pkg install` when the lockfile changes |
98	| Previewer wiring | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin]` | maps Office extensions → `piper -- view-office …` |
99	
100	`ya pkg install` **rewrites** `package.toml` (normalizes it and drops comments), so the managed source lockfile is kept **comment-free** to match its canonical output — that's what avoids chezmoi drift. It is install-only by design (like the rest of the repo) — bump plugin versions with `ya pkg upgrade` (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`), then copy the regenerated `~/.config/yazi/package.toml` back into the source.
101	
102	Add another yazi plugin:
103	
104	```bash
105	ya pkg add <owner>/<repo>:<plugin>       # installs + updates ~/.config/yazi/package.toml
106	cp ~/.config/yazi/package.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/yazi/package.toml)"
107	```
108	
109	## Where things live
110	
111	| Surface | Path |
112	|---|---|
113	| Dispatcher CLI | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office` |
114	| Completions (zsh/bash) | `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/55_view_office_completion.*` |
115	| doxx / LibreOffice install | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
116	| markitdown install | `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` |
117	| yazi previewers | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` |
118	| yazi plugin lockfile + installer | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` |
119	| Upgrades | `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`) |
120	
121	## Gotchas
122	
123	- **`markitdown` needs extras** — see the box above. `markitdown[docx,xlsx,pptx]`, not bare `markitdown`.
124	- **pandoc ≠ Office reader** — it cannot read `.pptx`/`.xlsx`. Use `markitdown` for those. (pandoc still powers the [web reader](web-reader.md) for HTML.)
125	- **Uppercase extensions** — the yazi `url` globs are lowercase (`*.docx`); a file named `Report.DOCX` won't trigger the previewer (running `view-office` directly still works — it lowercases internally).
126	- **LibreOffice cold start** — the first legacy-format conversion spins up a headless soffice profile (~1–2 s); previews of `.doc/.xls/.ppt` are slower than modern formats.
127	- **PATH in yazi previews** — `piper` runs the command via `sh`; `view-office` must be on the `PATH` yazi inherited. Launch yazi from a configured shell so `~/.dotfiles/bin` is present.
128	
129	## See also
130	
131	- [Data Viewers](../shells/aliases.md) — VisiData wrappers.
132	- [Web reader](web-reader.md) — read HTML pages as markdown (the pandoc/`glow` sibling).
133	- [tool-managers.md](../this_repo/tool-managers.md) — install-side index (doxx, markitdown, libreoffice, `ya pkg`).
134
```

I have concretely reproduced everything needed. Here is my adversarial verdict.

**The claimed defect (LibreOffice latency = "hang" / "blank preview") is NOT confirmed as a robustness defect** — but verifying it surfaced a genuinely worse, separate bug on the same path.

What I reproduced (`soffice` IS installed at `/usr/local/bin/soffice`; built a real 2-line legacy `.doc`):

1. **Latency is real (~7s), no caching** — matches the claim's order of magnitude (claim 8.19s, mine 6.7–7.1s across cold *and* warm runs; each hover spawns a fresh isolated soffice profile via `mktemp`, so warm runs don't speed up).
2. **It is NOT a hang.** Yazi runs previewers asynchronously (piper's `M:peek` uses `Command:spawn()` + `child:read_line()`); the UI never freezes and you can navigate away. "Reads as a hang" is subjective, not an actual hang/crash.
3. **It is NOT blank/silent-empty from the latency.** The conversion succeeds and doxx renders the real document text.
4. The claim's own recommendation is doc-level ("acceptable for CLI use", "document the cost"), and `docs/tools/office-viewers.md:126` already flags the cold-start cost — though it understates it (says ~1–2s; actual ~7s).

**The real bug I found while verifying** (higher priority than the claimed latency, and NOT what the claim describes): `render_legacy()` at `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office:162-179` does `local tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT`. Under the script's `set -euo pipefail`, the EXIT trap fires *after* `render_legacy` has returned, so `$tmp` is out of scope → `line 1: tmp: unbound variable`. Consequences, all reproduced:
- **exit code 1** even though rendering succeeded;
- **temp-dir leak on every hover** — the `rm -rf` never runs (confirmed +1 leaked LibreOffice profile+twin per invocation, delta +3 over 3 runs);
- **piper renders the error, not the content** — piper's `M:peek` (`~/.config/yazi/plugins/piper.yazi/main.lua:39-40`) shows *any* stderr as the whole preview and discards stdout. Faithful simulation confirms: for a legacy doc whose rendered text fits the pane height (short docs = common case), the yazi preview pane displays `view-office: line 1: tmp: unbound variable` after the 7s wait instead of the document. (Only docs longer than the pane height escape this, because piper stops reading at the line limit before the trailing stderr.)

Fix for the real bug: `trap 'rm -rf "${tmp:-}"' EXIT` (or hoist cleanup out of the function-local scope).

When the trap executes in the global scope, it tries to reference the function-local `$tmp` variable which no longer exists, triggering an "unbound variable" error that prevents the `rm -rf` command from running at all — leaving the temporary directory leaked on disk. Since piper captures stderr as the preview output, users see the bash error message instead of the rendered document content for shorter files that fit within the preview pane. So when the EXIT trap fires at shell termination, the function has already returned and `tmp` is out of scope—under `set -u`, trying to expand it throws an unbound variable error, preventing the cleanup from running. This is a real bug affecting the legacy document preview path (`.doc`, `.xls`, `.ppt`, `.odt`, `.ods`, `.odp`, `.rtf` files)—it shows an error instead of content for short documents and leaks temporary directories. The fix is to use parameter expansion like `${tmp:-}` in the trap so it safely expands to nothing when unset, or restructure the cleanup logic entirely.

But wait—using `${tmp:-}` only fixes the error message, not the actual leak. At EXIT, the `tmp` variable is out of scope, so `${tmp:-}` expands to empty, and `rm -rf ""` does nothing. The temp directory still isn't cleaned up. To fix both the error and the leak, the cleanup needs to happen while `tmp` is still in scope.

The original EXIT trap was meant for interactive mode—when the viewer runs as a child process and the user quits the TUI, the EXIT trap should fire and clean up. But since `tmp` is function-local, it's never accessible at EXIT, so the trap was always broken. The real solution is to make `tmp` global so the EXIT trap can actually access it. So the viewer runs as a child process and blocks until the user exits, which means I can do cleanup inline at the end of `render_legacy` instead of relying on the EXIT trap. This way, after the viewer returns, I clean up the temp directory before the function exits, which handles both preview and interactive modes cleanly.

I need the EXIT trap for safety to catch those error cases. The best approach is to declare `tmp` as a global variable and use `trap 'rm -rf "${tmp:-}"' EXIT` so the cleanup always runs when the script exits, whether normally or via error.
